Wider Sports News.title: Benfica invests in education with creation of Benfica Institute for Sport Excellence
Wider Sports News.summary: Knowledge-sharing hub unveiled, with first course already underway, to underline the club's commitment to sporting excellence The post Benfica invests in education with creation of Benfica Institute for Sport Excellence appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Lisbon, September 8th, 2026 — Sport Lisboa e Benfica officially launched the Benfica Institute for Sport Excellence, a living knowledge-sharing hub that reflects a significant investment by the club in education and the sharing of its world renowned methodology and elite expertise with the wider sporting world, spanning talent development, applied research, innovation and specialist training for the football and sports industry.

The Institute will operate as an open platform for education, research and innovation aimed primarily at professionals and students seeking to work in sports, comprising six courses taught in Portuguese and English. Teaching staff are drawn largely from Benfica’s own football and sporting structure, alongside international university lecturers and sports scientists. Courses combine online and in-person formats, with in-person sessions held at Benfica Campus and Estádio da Luz.

Wider Sports News.title: Formula 1 has won the battle for attention. Now it needs to win the battle for loyalty.
Wider Sports News.summary: F1 has mastered the art of attracting a new generation of fans — but turning that surge in attention into lasting loyalty will be the defining challenge for teams, sponsors and the sport itself. The post Formula 1 has won the battle for attention. Now it needs to win the battle for loyalty. appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Bernie Ecclestone once dismissed social media as “nonsense”. He said he would rather chase the 70-year-old with money to spend than worry about building a younger audience online. It feels slightly mad now, given what Formula 1 has become.

When Liberty Media took over in 2017, the sport had a problem. TV audiences had been heading in the wrong direction and there was very little sense of where the next generation of fans would come from. The racing was still there, but F1 had spent years making itself strangely difficult to get close to.

Wider Sports News.title: World Rugby confirms LA28 Sevens Qualification Path
Wider Sports News.summary: World Rugby confirms LA28 Sevens Qualification Path Talking Rugby Union
Wider Sports News.body:
World Rugby has confirmed the qualification pathway for rugby sevens at the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games, with 12 men’s and 12 women’s teams set to compete. Host nation USA will receive automatic places in both competitions.

The qualification race will begin during the HSBC SVNS 2027 season, starting in Dubai in November 2026 and concluding in Bordeaux at the end of May 2027. The four highest-ranked eligible men’s teams and four highest-ranked eligible women’s teams in the final World Championship standings, excluding hosts USA, will qualify directly for LA28.

Wider Sports News.title: Consortium led by L Catterton in partnership with HYROX founders acquires Infront’s majority stake in HYROX
Wider Sports News.summary: HYROX’s rapid rise from emerging fitness format to global mass-participation phenomenon has opened the door to its next phase of growth, with ambitions spanning millions more participants, new products and a potential Olympic future. The post Consortium led by L Catterton in partnership with HYROX founders acquires Infront’s majority stake in HYROX appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
LONDON / ZUG, September 8th, 2026 – Infront Sports & Media AG (Infront), the leading international sports business company, today announced the completion of the sale of its majority stake in HYROX to a consortium led by L Catterton, the largest global consumer-focused investment firm, alongside HYROX founders Christian Toetzke and Moritz Fürste. WndrCo, the investment firm founded and led by Jeffrey Katzenburg and his partner Sujay Jaswa, will also participate in the transaction. This marks an important milestone in HYROX’s continued growth. Financial terms were not disclosed.

HYROX was created by Christian Toetzke, an industry veteran in the international cycling and triathlon world, and Moritz Fürste, one of Germany’s greatest ever field hockey players and successful entrepreneur. In less than a decade HYROX has become a global phenomenon including events, training programmes and affiliate gyms around the world that together deliver a competition format that inspires and unites athletes. The new partnership brings together HYROX’s category-defining brand and community with L Catterton’s extensive experience scaling high-growth consumer and fitness businesses around the world. Together, the founders and L Catterton will continue to invest in delivering an exceptional experience for HYROX athletes and the development of Hybrid Racing as a global sport.

Wider Sports News.title: “I sold at the lowest”: Andrea Radrizzani on his Leeds mistake, DAZN exit timeline and where he’s investing next
Wider Sports News.summary: Armed with experiences at MP & Silva, Leeds United and Aser Ventures, Andrea Radrizzani tells SportsPro where the real value now lies for investors. The post “I sold at the lowest”: Andrea Radrizzani on his Leeds mistake, DAZN exit timeline and where he’s investing next appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Leeds United’s fanbase has a reputation for being one of the most loyal in English soccer. Andrea Radrizzani learned that quickly when he bought the club for UK£45 million (US$61 million) in 2017. The Italian was already well known within sports industry circles as the co-founder of MP & Silva, the now-defunct international media rights agency he established in 2004 before selling his shares in 2016, when the company had reached a US$1 billion valuation. Leeds, however, represented his first move into soccer club ownership.

Some investors might have preferred to cut their teeth at a smaller club before taking over one of the best-followed teams in England. However, after hearing Liverpool great Kenny Dalglish refer to Leeds as a sleeping giant, the opportunity to bring success back to one of soccer’s true one-club cities proved too good to turn down for Radrizzani, who has described himself as an underdog in business.

Jesus ‘Chus’ Bueno would like to have started earlier. As it is, the Euroleague Basketball chief executive has taken his post at what might be the most pivotal moment for the organisation since its creation 26 years ago.

Transformation looms for Euroleague and for basketball. Internally, Bueno is working through a profound commercial and financial restructuring that he hopes will unlock fresh potential. Wider Sports News.title: ”Invest in Ukraine”: Rinat Akhmetov’s SCM issues a global call to international community for UEFA Champions League season
Wider Sports News.summary: Shakhtar Donetsk is turning its Champions League presence into a platform for economic diplomacy, using football’s global reach to encourage international investment in Ukraine and reinforce the case for rebuilding while the war continues. The post ”Invest in Ukraine”: Rinat Akhmetov’s SCM issues a global call to international community for UEFA Champions League season appeared first on SportsPro .
Wider Sports News.body:
Kyiv, August 31, 2026 – Ukraine’s largest private investor — Rinat Akhmetov’s System Capital Management (SCM) companies — is launching a global communications initiative calling on international business to invest in Ukraine. As part of the initiative, Shakhtar Donetsk Football Club will play the league phase of the 2026/2027 UEFA Champions League in shirts carrying the call to “Invest in Ukraine.”

The league phase of the UEFA Champions League is one of the world’s most prominent sporting platforms, attracting one of the largest audiences. The club will play at least eight matches against leading European clubs, while the Ukrainian champions will host their home matches in London — one of the world’s financial capitals.

Rugby.title: Shujaa, Lionesses eye LA28 rugby sevens via African qualifier
Rugby.summary: Shujaa, Lionesses eye LA28 rugby sevens via African qualifier The Eastleigh Voice
Rugby.body:

Rugby.title: Why Cardiff is the perfect place to kick off Ultimate Sevens
Rugby.summary: Even within the long list of internationally renowned rugby cauldrons, the Cardiff Arms Park precinct in Wales’ capital holds a unique place.
Rugby.body:
Even within the long list of internationally renowned rugby cauldrons, the Cardiff Arms Park precinct in Wales’ capital holds a unique place. As it prepares to re-enter the world of sevens rugby for the first time in over a decade with the launch of the Ultimate Sevens, the new competition is set to tread on hallowed ground, and it could not have picked a more appropriate place to acknowledge rugby’s past.

Sport in many forms has been played in the precinct along the River Taff for nearly 200 years, the original field starting out as a site for cricket matches in the 1850s. By the 1880s, rugby had arrived, the area converted into a cricket ground to the north (the site of today’s ground where the Ultimate Sevens will be played) and a rugby union ground to the south, the current home of Millennium Stadium.

Rugby.title: Pia Tapsell: 'I’d be lying if I said I wasn’t a little worried about the reception'
Rugby.summary: The Black Ferns' euphoric 2022 season was a nightmare for Pia Tapsell.
Rugby.body:
The Black Ferns’ euphoric 2022 season was a nightmare for Pia Tapsell. The abrasive loose forward who started all six Tests in a successful 2019, when the Black Ferns defeated England 28-13 in San Diego en route to a Super Series title, missed selection for the Women’s Rugby World Cup. A serious ACL injury ruled her out for all of 2023.

A slow recovery and desire for a new challenge led her to move to Australia. On August 22 at North Harbour Stadium in Albany, she became the first woman to play a Test match for both the Black Ferns and the Wallaroos when she came off the bench for Australia in the last half hour of their 66-19 defeat.

Rugby.body:
Lloyds Bank’s iconic black horse was front and centre of the RFU’s announcement of their new back-of-shirt sponsor on Wednesday, but it’s very presence is all thanks to a winger who won one cap against Scotland 56 years ago.

Mike Bulpitt was born in Richmond, Yorkshire, in April 1944 and played for Blackheath, Eastern Counties, Rosslyn Park, London Counties and the Barbarians. He worked for the ad agency Coleman Prentice & Varley before joining Lloyds Bank as Assistant Advertising Manager, where he developed the bank’s famous ‘Black Horse’ campaign. He was chief manager of marketing communications when he retired.

Rugby.title: Club-by-club Top 14 salary cap figures revealed for 2026/27 season
Rugby.summary: With the Top14 already underway, the Ligue Nationale de Rugby has released the salary cap figures for each club for the 2026/2027 season.
Rugby.body:
With the Top14 already underway, the Ligue Nationale de Rugby has released the salary cap figures for each club for the 2026/2027 season. The competition’s base budget is €11.1 million, a figure that may increase depending on how many players are involved with the French national 15s and 7s squads.

The reigning champions, Stade Toulousain, have the largest salary cap budget in the competition, reaching €13.8 million, which is driven by the club having 16 players who have represented the French national team in the past season – 15 in the 15s and one in the 7s.

Rugby.title: 'Talent, neglect and deprivation'
Rugby.summary: Through apartheid, poverty and financial crises, this special province continues to defy the odds, but investment is needed to stop it being left behind.
Rugby.body:
Around the jagged cliffs of Coffee Bay, the Wild Coast earns its name. Undulating green hills plunge from great heights into a frothing sea. Fat oysters cling to the surf-battered rocks. The sandy beaches are vast, the water brilliant and the views staggering.

The roads in and out are less romantic. They turn to porridge when it rains and are pocked with potholes beneath the baking sun. Coffee Bay is a place that can take your breath away, provided you are only passing through.

Rugby.title: Rob Baxter assesses Tommy Wyatt after two years of injury hell
Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter admits he was delighted to see full-back Tommy Wyatt put almost two years of injury hell behind him and is now ready to accelerate his progress ahead of the new season.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter admits he was delighted to see full-back Tommy Wyatt put almost two years of injury hell behind him and is now ready to accelerate his progress ahead of the new season.

Wyatt played 40 minutes of a pre-season game against the Scarlets last weekend, his first game in over a year after suffering a second serious knee ligament injury. Baxter says that, as expected for someone who has been out of action for such a long period, Wyatt made some errors as he shook off the rust.

Rugby.title: ‘The All Blacks are back… and they are most certainly World Cup contenders’
Rugby.summary: Despite falling 2-1 down in their series with South Africa, New Zealand have shown they are good enough to challenge for global glory in 2027.
Rugby.body:
Regardless of how the last Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series plays out, there is enough reason now to be confident that the All Blacks are back. They are the All Blacks again. Behaving like them, training like them, preparing like them and playing like them. Once again, New Zealand are a genuine threat to every team they play and good enough to beat everyone on any given day.

They are, most certainly, World Cup contenders and just how strong a chance they are of winning in Australia depends on how far they progress along their current trajectory in the next 12 months.

Rugby.title: Red Roses record try-scorer among the latest World Rugby Hall of Fame inductees.
Rugby.summary: Red Roses record try-scorer Sue Day is among the latest five World Rugby Hall of Fame inductees.
Rugby.body:
Red Roses record try-scorer Sue Day is among the latest five World Rugby Hall of Fame inductees. During a 10-year career with the Red Roses, Day scored 61 tries for England, including 19 at three Women’s Rugby World Cups. A tally only bettered by that of Portia Woodman-Wickliffe.

She also captained the Red Roses to one of the three Women’s Six Nations titles claimed during her career. Since retirement, Day has been appointed the first-ever female president of Wasps FC and as a partner at her accountancy firm.

Rugby.summary: Lloyds will become the first-ever back-of-the-shirt sponsor for both the England men's and women's senior teams after signing a multi-year agreement to become the the Official Banking Partner of England Rugby.
Rugby.body:
Lloyds will become the first-ever back-of-the-shirt sponsor for both the England men’s and women’s senior teams after signing a multi-year agreement to become the the Official Banking Partner of England Rugby.

The partnership will see Lloyds and the RFU work together in initiatives designed to “improve the long-term sustainability of local grassroots clubs, enhance community facilities, and introduce tens of thousands of young people to the sport.”

Rugby.title: Report: RFU ready to stick by Steve Borthwick beyond Rugby World Cup 2027
Rugby.summary: He has won 57.4% of his Tests (28/48) as head coach since succeeding Eddie Jones, and will join double Grand Slam winner and fellow northerner Geoff Cooke on 50 Tests when England play Japan in November.
Rugby.body:
Steve Borthwick is set to be awarded a contract extension by the RFU through to 2028, according to a report in The Telegraph today. The 46-year-old Lancastrian first took charge of England ahead of the 2023 Six Nations, and led them to the semi-finals of that year’s Rugby World Cup.

He has won 57.4% of his Tests (28/48) as head coach since succeeding Eddie Jones, and will join double Grand Slam winner and fellow northerner Geoff Cooke on 50 Tests when England play Japan on Saturday, 14 November, at Allianz Stadium.

Rugby.title: How backpacking Europe put NZ-raised prospect on path to Canada Test rugby
Rugby.summary: Spencer Jones has played 18 Test matches and the centre has been named in Canada's squad for the Asahi Super Rugby Pacific Nations Cup.
Rugby.body:
Vancouver-born Spencer Jones spent his teenage years living in New Zealand, coming through the rugby age-grade ranks in Waikato before opting to take a break from the sport. It was a choice that led to life-changing opportunities and “sparked that love again” for rugby.

Jones has played 18 Test matches for Canada and the midfielder has been named in the 32-player squad for the Asahi Super Rugby Pacific Nations Cup 2026. But the journey to this point has spanned multiple countries and took a dramatic turn during a solo backpacking trip through Europe.

Rugby.body:
Amy Williams' international rugby debut was the stuff of sporting dreams. The 21-year-old from Pontypool lined up on the wing against a Barbarians side littered with global superstars and ran in two tries in a rare Welsh win at Twickenham.

"I was just in shock," said Williams. "It's my favourite moment of my sporting career so far. I couldn't believe it when I scored." Scoring is not unfamiliar territory to Williams.

Rugby.body:
Exeter boss Rob Baxter hopes full-back Tommy Wyatt can return to his best form after overcoming his second serious knee injury. The 26-year-old returned to action last weekend in Exeter's pre-season friendly loss to Scarlets at Sandy Park, where he played the first half.

He missed the entirety of last season after rupturing the anterior cruciate ligament in his left knee in the final game of the 2024-25 campaign. Wyatt had missed much of 2024 having suffered a similar injury in his other knee.

Rugby.title: Rugby Union Weekly
Rugby.summary: Ugo and Chris chat to RFU performance director Conor O'Shea.
Rugby.body: Ugo and Chris sit down with the RFU performance director Conor O’Shea for a wide-ranging conversation about the big issues shaping English rugby. O’Shea reveals they plan to extend Steve Borthwick’s contract to cover the 2028 Six Nations and prevent speculation around his future. They discuss the importance of the upcoming autumn and despite a poor 2026 O’Shea tells us England can go all the way at the 2027 World Cup in Australia. Should the RFU scrap the rule preventing overseas-based players being picked for England? And how do they improve the coaching pathway for English coaches to make the jump from domestic to international rugby? They also quiz O’Shea on the Red Roses’ dominance and the succession plan for John Mitchell.

Rugby.summary: The 27 Test All Blacks prop is on an upward trajectory to return to the Christchurch-based Super Rugby Pacific franchise in 2027.
Rugby.body:
Injured All Blacks prop Tamaiti Williams has provided an update on his recovery from a serious back injury during the Crusaders’ 2026 Super Rugby Pacific season. The 26-year-old played 104 minutes for the Crusaders in 2026, missing the rest of the Super Rugby Pacific campaign and the international season to date.

Williams was suspended after their round three clash with the Chiefs, before his week off was cut short by severe back pain. While the initial injury seemed minor, as the weeks went by, Williams was forced into hospital for a chunk of time over a couple of months.

Rugby.summary: Uganda steps up preparations to host World Rugby Sevens qualifiers The Eastleigh Voice
Rugby.body:
Uganda has stepped up preparations to host a qualification tournament for the 2027 World Rugby Sevens Series. The two-day tournament, scheduled for September 26-27, will feature eight teams and serve as the opening leg of the 2026/2027 men's World Rugby Sevens qualifying series.

Godwin Kayangwe, president of the Uganda Rugby Union (URU), told Xinhua on Monday that the union was working closely with the government to ensure the tournament's success. "We are confident that Uganda will host an excellent tournament and we are preparing well for it," added Kayangwe.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: Scotland
Rugby.summary: When the WXV Global Series fixtures were first being arranged, Scotland would have been delighted to secure fixtures versus Canada and New Zealand at home first up.
Rugby.body:
When the WXV Global Series fixtures were first being arranged, Scotland would have been delighted to secure fixtures versus Canada and New Zealand at home first up. After all, those sides are lying number three and number two in the world ranking respectively at time of writing, will bring the crowds flocking to Hive Stadium in Edinburgh and Canada were last in Scotland in 2018 and the Black Ferns have never played in the country.

Both games will certainly be glamour days and big occasions for women’s rugby in Scotland that’s for sure, but fast forward a few months since the fixtures were made public and the Scots might fancy a slightly less taxing start to their five-game September and October schedule.

Rugby.title: 2026 WXV Global Series preview: The Wallaroos
Rugby.summary: Of all the teams taking part in the WXV Global Series, the Wallaroos come into September in one of the most intriguing positions in all of international women’s rugby.
Rugby.body:
Of all the teams taking part in the WXV Global Series, the Wallaroos come into September in one of the most intriguing positions in all of international women’s rugby. These eight weeks will mark the final time the Wallaroos take the field as semi-professional athletes – with XVs players joining their sevens counterparts in a full-time, high-performance environment from November.

Led by the new Head of Women’s High Performance, Tim Walsh, morale on the ground is high: with the Australia Sevenss winning the 2026 HSBC SVNS World Championship and the governing body having one eye on the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles and Women’s Rugby World Cup 2029 on home soil.

Rugby.body:

The North London side have been crowned back-to-back champions twice in the last decade, and England A back-rower Pearson, 26, knows nine clubs will be looking to knock Saints off their perch.

Pearson believes Saints, who have won two of the last three PREM finals at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium, will be helped in their quest to become top dogs again after keeping most of their squad intact.

A wealth of talented players remain out of reach for England boss Steve Borthwick because they play in France, most notably Toulouse stars Jack Willis and his brother Tom, and the Toulon duo Kyle Sinckler and Lewis Ludlam.

Rugby.title: Springbok Women ‘established credibility’ despite loss to Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: Springbok Women co-coach Laurian Johannes-Haupt believes her side “established credibility” despite a 52-20 defeat to the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Springbok Women co-coach Laurian Johannes-Haupt believes her side “established credibility” despite a 52-20 defeat to the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium. For the opening 30 minutes in the curtain-raiser to Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’s third Test, the Springbok Women were well in the contest. Their forward pack posed physical questions to Whitney Hansen’s team.

It was not quite the effort of their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 exploits against the same opposition. Almost a year ago South Africa went in level with the Black Ferns at the break. This time around New Zealand led 24-10.

Rugby.title: Not 'boring'
Rugby.summary: Dan McFarland arrived in the North East this summer after winning the Japanese Top League title with Kobelco Steelers.
Rugby.body:
Dan McFarland is honest enough to admit he doesn’t know what his new-look Newcastle Red Bulls squad, with 23 new signings, can achieve this season. McFarland arrived in the North East this summer after winning the Japanese Top League title with Kobelco Steelers and is trying to mould a squad that he hopes will be able to climb off the foot of the Gallagher PREM table.

The Red Bulls have won only four PREM games in three seasons, so the task is huge, but at least McFarland is honest enough not to set unrealistic goals for his side, saying it has all the feel of a start-up project.

Rugby.summary: Former Wales and Lions wing Shane Williams says pathways support for schools and colleges from the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) is 'almost non-existent'.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales and British and Irish Lions wing Shane Williams says financial support for schools and colleges rugby from the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU) is "almost non-existent". Wales' record try scorer is head of rugby at Ysgol Dyffryn Aman and suggests that support is reserved for elite players tied to regions.

The 49-year-old warns that good players are being lost because of a lack of WRU investment in student pathways. "It's the most important part of it all," Williams told Radio Wales Breakfast.

Rugby.title: John Smit makes huge all-time Malcolm Marx claim ahead of All Blacks finale
Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain John Smit has declared Malcolm Marx not only the best player in the world, but the greatest hooker to have ever played for the Springboks.
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain John Smit has declared Malcolm Marx not only the best player in the world, but the greatest hooker to have ever played for the Springboks. Marx was again influential in South Africa’s latest win over the All Blacks, producing a near-complete display in the 29-24 victory in Johannesburg. His lineout throwing was faultless, he won a crucial breakdown penalty and scored off a driving maul late on as the world champions opened up a 2-1 lead in the four-match series against New Zealand.

The 32-year-old has become one of the defining figures of this Springbok era, and Smit, himself a World Cup-winning hooker, believes Marx now stands above every South African to have previously worn the jersey.

Rugby.title: Quirke excited by 'new project' at Newcastle
Rugby.summary: Raffi Quirke says leaving Sale Sharks was one of the hardest decisions he has had to make, but is impressed with how things are taking shape at a revamped Newcastle Red Bulls.
Rugby.body:
Scrum-half Raffi Quirke says that leaving Sale Sharks was one of the hardest decisions he has ever had to make, but has been impressed with how things are taking shape at a revamped Newcastle Red Bulls.

Quirke is one of 25 new arrivals at Kingston Park, with the Red Bull ownership looking to improve on a team which has finished bottom of the table for the past four seasons. The move north means stepping away from his boyhood side and familiar surroundings, but the 25-year-old is excited by the challenge of pushing Newcastle forward in a new era for the club.

Rugby.title: England Rugby announce addition to November fixture schedule
Rugby.summary: International rugby is returning to Bath, with The Recreation Ground set to host England A vs Argentina XV on Friday, 6 November.
Rugby.body:
International rugby is returning to Bath, with The Recreation Ground set to host England A vs Argentina XV on Friday, 6 November, kick off 19:45pm (GMT). It will be the first meeting between each union’s development sides since 2009 and the third overall. England ‘A’ previously beat Argentina ‘A’ 22-17 at Franklin’s Gardens in December 1996 and again in the Churchill Cup in Colorado in June 2009 (28-20).

Argentina XV are currently licking their wounds after losing their Americas Rugby Championship crown to Chile at the weekend. Since being reintroduced in 2024, England A have played six fixtures, with five wins and a defeat. That loss was 12 months ago in England A’s only previous outing at The Rec, with the All Blacks XV winning 31-14.

Rugby.summary: Rob Baxter has tipped 22-year-old centre Zack Wimbush for a big season as Exeter Chiefs look to fill the void left by Len Ikitau at Sandy Park ahead of the new Gallagher PREM campaign.
Rugby.body:
Rob Baxter has tipped 22-year-old centre Zack Wimbush for a breakthrough season as Exeter Chiefs look to fill the void left by Len Ikitau at Sandy Park ahead of the new Gallagher PREM campaign.

The 112kg centre, who qualifies for both England and Wales, was largely limited to PREM Cup appearances last season alongside a loan spell with Plymouth Albion. But after what Baxter has described as a “very, very good pre-season”, the Exeter boss expects him to kick on this term.

Rugby.title: Four lessons Australia need to learn from Argentina series ‘win’
Rugby.summary: Despite starting his tenure with an unbeaten run of four Tests, Les Kiss's Wallabies will need to be a lot better in the tougher assignments next up.
Rugby.body:
Coaches love to say you learn far more from a loss than a win, and even more again from a close loss. But despite starting his tenure as Australia coach with an unbeaten run that now extends to four Tests across two mini-series, Les Kiss will have collected pages of lessons from the Wallabies’ tour of Argentina.

Clearly, there’s some tough outings coming up next and it’s not an earth-shattering revelation to suggest they will need to be a lot better than we’ve seen over the last six weeks with South Africa up next, then New Zealand twice, before four more Nations Championship matches in November – England, Scotland, Wales, plus a play-off match.

Rugby.title: Ex-Wales captain secures ‘key’ WRU development role
Rugby.summary: Former Wales captain Siwan Lillicrap has been appointed head of women's coaching and development by the Welsh Rugby Union.
Rugby.body:
Former Wales captain Siwan Lillicrap has been appointed head of women’s coaching and development by the Welsh Rugby Union. The role, which has been newly created, is one that the WRU have described as “key” and “acknowledges the rapid growth of the women’s and girls’ game globally”. It is also forms part of the WRU’s ‘One Wales’ strategy.

During a six year international career, Lillicrap won 51 caps for Wales and has been Pathway Manager for the three Player Development Centres established by the WRU in Wast Wales, West Wales and North Wales since 2023. She was also Wales Women’s Under-18s head coach.

Rugby.title: Historic result in South America as Chile complete stunning comeback
Rugby.summary: This year marked the return of the Americas Rugby Championship, which had been forced into a long hiatus due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
Rugby.body:
The 2026 Americas Rugby Championship concluded at the weekend, and Chile XV took the title home after successfully defeating Uruguay XV, Paraguay and Argentina XV. This year marked the return of the tournament, which had been forced into a long hiatus due to the COVID-19 pandemic; Argentina XV won the last edition held in 2019.

While Chile, Uruguay and Argentina competed with their secondary sides, the Cóndores and Los Teros still fielded several of their main players, including Chilean siblings Santiago and Benjamín Videla and Uruguayan back-rower Manuel Diana.

Rugby.title: Ollie Blyth-Lafferty: 'I had my plumber's tool bag ready to go, then Edinburgh offered me a contract'
Rugby.summary: The 135kg would-be plumber is only 20, but has all the raw materials to become the cornterstone of Scotland's pack in the years ahead.
Rugby.body:
Had things turned out a little differently, Ollie Blyth-Lafferty would be servicing boilers instead of grinding at the coalface of rugby’s least forgiving frontier. The enormous tighthead prop, who thundered onto the URC scene last season, had his heart set on becoming a plumber before rugby jolted suddenly from hobby to career path. In the past nine months, the 20-year-old has signed his first professional contract, captained Scotland U20s, and played 15 games for Edinburgh, four of them in the Champions Cup. His first start came in a sterling win opposite Toulon’s gnarled loosehead Jean-Baptiste Gros. His immense 6ft 4ins, 135kg frame is a precious rarity in Scotland. His clear zest for scrummaging and the dearth of options to back up Zander Fagerson have fuelled clamour for him to be capped at Test level. The mending of leaks and unclogging of toilets, then, can wait.

“I was planning on leaving school at 16 to do plumbing and heating,” Blyth-Lafferty says. “I had a start day lined up, I had my own tool bag ready to go, and then I got offered a senior academy contract with Edinburgh and that was full time. I couldn’t go into plumbing.

Rugby.summary: Desiree Miller believes the Aussies can go into their WXV Global Series opener against England with a nothing-to-lose mentality.
Rugby.body:
Record-setting Wallaroos winger Desiree Miller believes the Aussies can go into their WXV Global Series opener against England with a nothing-to-lose mentality, as they look to take down the “gold standard” side in women’s 15s rugby.

England were beaten in the 2022 Women’s Rugby World Cup Final against New Zealand at Eden Park, but have gone unbeaten since then. The Red Roses stormed home to win the World Cup on home soil last year, and backed that up with more Six Nations success.

Rugby.title: RC Vannes: The beating heart of Bretagne set on joining the French elite
Rugby.summary: The first Breton club to win promotion to the Top 14 two years ago, Vannes are determined to make their new stay in the premier division last.
Rugby.body:
If you happen to be strolling by the Rue du Port in Vannes on a matchday, you might hear a chant sung in unison from the La Rabine stadium that will make your soul tingle. For rugby fans, while the lyrics may be unfamiliar, the melody itself will carry resonance. This is the ‘Bro Gozh ma Zadoù’, the Breton version of ‘Land of My Fathers’, Vannes and Bretagne’s official anthem which shares a common link with Wales.

Vannes, one of the oldest towns in France, first established by the Veneti, a Gallic tribe from BC times, harbours some of the most passionate and humble people and rugby clubs you will ever come across.

Rugby.summary: Rennie isn't shying away from the facts surrounding the set-piece, but knows there are areas where the All Blacks can improve.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie has admitted his All Blacks side is still showing signs of growing pains in both the lineout and scrum battles, where they have been tested heavily during Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry Tour.

Rassie Erasmus’ Springboks have been ferocious and clinical at set-piece when handed the opportunities, taking advantage of the All Blacks’ indiscretions around the field. The 62-year-old All Blacks head coach explained to media in Washington, DC, and on the DSPN Podcast that his side’s inexperienced players will be better off after the gruelling seven-week tour of the Republic.

Former World Rugby Player of the Year nominee Joe Taufete’e is among the 30 Major League Rugby players named in the USA squad for the 2026 Pacific Nations Cup, which kicks off this weekend with a double-header in Osaka.

Rugby.title: Trying to withstand the Springboks shove is not working
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks on the other hand, are trying to withstand the shove, a passive approach. They want a stable platform and are trying to bunker down and withstand the heat.
Rugby.body:
The third Test between the All Blacks and Springboks once again highlighted the key difference at scrum time, which proved to be an advantage for South Africa. They won four penalties off the scrum, rewarded for their dominance, which put the spotlight back on the All Blacks’ ball handling.

Every knock-on is amplified against South Africa; the clock is lost and 30-40 metres of territory nearly every time when a penalty is conceded. You don’t just lose possession; you lose pressure, territory and momentum as well.

Rugby.summary: The Springboks have named their 23 to play the All Blacks in Baltimore, sticking firm with most of the starting team that secured a 2-1 lead at FNB Stadium.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks have named their 23 to play the All Blacks in Baltimore, sticking firm with most of the starting team that secured a 2-1 lead at FNB Stadium. Damian Willemse comes back into the starting team at fullback to replace Cheslin Kolbe, who was forced off early in the third Test. Willemse himself came off in the second Test with a hamstring issue.

Scrumhalf Morne van den Berg has been handed a start in the halves next to Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu, with Cobus Reinach moving to the bench. The forward pack remains unchanged with Ox Nche, Malcolm Marx and Wilco Louw in the front row, Eben Etzebeth and Ruan Nortje in the second row and captain Siya Kolisi, Pieter-Steph du Toit and Jasper Wiese in the back row.

Rugby.title: Wales drop to lowest-ever position in the World Rugby rankings
Rugby.summary: Wales have dropped to their lowest-ever position in the World Rugby rankings after Fiji beat Japan last weekend.
Rugby.body:
Wales have dropped to their lowest-ever position in the World Rugby rankings after Fiji beat Japan last weekend. On Friday afternoon in Fukuoka, Willie Walker’s Fijiana XV were able to grind out a 15-12 win against their hosts, the Sakura Fifteen and overtake the side they stunned in the group stage of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

The result means that Fiji have moved to a new high of 12th in the World Rugby rankings, while Wales have fallen to their lowest ranking ever [13th]. Wales have not won a Test since July 2025, when they overcame Australia 21-12 in Brisbane. At Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 Sean Lynn’s team went winless and concluded the tournament with a 28-25 loss to Fiji. In the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations the side picked up a third wooden spoon in a row.
Rugby.copy:

On Friday afternoon in Fukuoka, Willie Walker’s Fijiana XV were able to grind out a 15-12 win against their hosts, the Sakura Fifteen and overtake the side they stunned in the group stage of Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025.

The result means that Fiji have moved to a new high of 12th in the World Rugby rankings, while Wales have fallen to their lowest ranking ever [13th]. Wales have not won a Test since July 2025, when they overcame Australia 21-12 in Brisbane. At Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 Sean Lynn’s team went winless and concluded the tournament with a 28-25 loss to Fiji. In the 2026 Guinness Women’s Six Nations the side picked up a third wooden spoon in a row.

Rugby.title: Allow overseas stars to play for England
Rugby.summary: England selection should no longer be restricted to players based at domestic clubs, according to cap centurion Courtney Lawes.
Rugby.body:
England selection should no longer be restricted to players based at domestic clubs, according to cap centurion Courtney Lawes. The 37-year-old is back in contention to add to his 105 England appearances, having signed a one-year deal with Sale after two seasons at Brive in the French second tier.

A clutch of English talent - notably Toulouse star Jack Willis - remain across the Channel and out of reach for England head coach Steve Borthwick. "I can see why they do it because they don't want all their players playing abroad, but I don't think that's necessarily going to be the case anyway," said Lawes.

Rugby.title: WRU appoints Lillicrap to new women's role
Rugby.summary: Former captain Siwan Lillicrap is named head of women's coaching and development by the Welsh Rugby Union.
Rugby.body:
Former captain Siwan Lillicrap has been appointed as head of women's coaching and development by the Welsh Rugby Union (WRU). WRU chiefs say Lillicrap will "deliver an aligned coaching and development system across the women's performance pathway for players between 14 and 24 years of age" in the newly created role.

Lillicrap, who won 51 Wales caps, has worked as WRU's pathway manager and women's under-18s head coach since retiring from international rugby in 2022. In her role as pathways manager, the 38-year-old oversaw player development centres in east, west and north Wales.

Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter points out that new owners Black Knight Entertainment haven’t just come into Sandy Park with a blank chequebook...
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter points out that new owners Black Knight Entertainment haven’t just come into Sandy Park with a blank chequebook but are expecting the club to return to being a well-run, profitable business.

Baxter says that Bill Foley’s summer investment in the club has lifted the financial strain on the club, which was once the most profitable club in the Gallagher Prem before the pandemic wrecked its finances.

Rugby.title: Four-time PWR winner commits to 13th Saracens season
Rugby.summary: Lotte Sharp has re-signed with Saracens to take her association with the North London club into a 13th season.
Rugby.body:
Lotte Sharp has re-signed with Saracens to take her association with the North London club into a 13th season. The 31-year-old joined Saracens in 2014 from Welwyn Rugby and won the Women’s Premiership in her first season.

In the years since, Sharp has since made her 150th appearance for the club and has won JAECOO Premiership Women’s Rugby four times. Last season Sharp made 15 league appearances for the StoneX Stadium club and scored five tries. In addition to playing top-flight rugby, Sharp teaches full-time at Heath Mount School.

Rugby.summary: Leicester Tigers scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet admits that watching arch East Midland rivals Northampton Saints dancing around Twickenham, celebrating winning the Gallagher Prem left a bitter taste.
Rugby.body:
Leicester Tigers scrum-half Jack van Poortvliet admits that watching arch East Midland rivals Northampton Saints dancing around Twickenham, celebrating winning the Gallagher Prem left a bitter taste.

Especially so after Saints beat them 45-31 in the PREM semi-finals to book their place in the showpiece, but the England star says that the Tigers, who won the PREM Rugby Cup last season, will be chasing that winning feeling themselves this season.

Rugby.title: Henry Pollock contract call a win for everyone – Andy Goode
Rugby.summary: Henry Pollock’s new contract at Northampton represents a win for everyone, even if it might not be worth the million pound a year that Eddie Hearn was after.
Rugby.body:
Henry Pollock’s new contract at Northampton represents a win for everyone, even if it might not be worth the million pounds a year that Eddie Hearn was after. Let’s face it, the reported Newcastle offer came about because I don’t think anyone expects him to move abroad at his age and they’re the only club in the PREM who could offer him anywhere near that amount of money.

Pollock wants to win things, develop his own game and make an even bigger impression on the international stage though, as well as earning as much as possible along the way, and there’s absolutely no doubt that Saints is the right place for him.

Rugby.summary: The fly-half entered the fray after Cheslin Kolbe broke his jaw, and turned the Springboks from ball winners to ball users against the All Blacks.
Rugby.body:
A traditional proverb: “better to be lucky than good”. Even at the elite level of sporting performance, where every ‘i’ is dotted and every ‘t’ is crossed, sometimes you need to catch a lucky break for all the preparation to count. Life can be that simple.

As the American crooner Frank Sinatra once observed, “people often remark I’m pretty lucky. Luck is only important insofar as getting the chance to sell yourself at the right moment. After that, you’ve got to have talent and know how to use it.”

Rugby.title: Where does PREM Cup points-fest rank in rugby's highest-scoring matches?
Rugby.summary: It was a truly remarkable opening weekend of the PREM Rugby Cup, with an aggregate of 365 points scored across the four matches.
Rugby.body:
It was a truly remarkable opening weekend of the PREM Rugby Cup, with an aggregate of 365 points scored across the four matches. On any other weekend, the point-a-minute, 43-40 thriller between Bristol and Gloucester, won by the Bears, would have likely eclipsed all others as a free-for-all.

But at the same time as they were going at each other hammer and tongs in the west, Saracens and Northampton served up a scoreline that was barely believable. Twenty tries were scored – 14 to Saracens and six to Northampton – with young Jack Bracken claiming a nine-minute hat-trick.

Rugby.summary: Charlie Bracken, son of RWC 2003 winner and fellow scrum-half Kyran, has been called into this week's three-day alignment camp.
Rugby.body:
Charlie Bracken, son of RWC 2003 winner and fellow scrum-half Kyran, has been called into England’s three-day alignment camp after Archie McParland was forced to withdraw due to illness.

Bracken, 22, was a regular starter for England U20s in 2022 and 2023 and is now on Steve Borthwick’s radar for the senior team. He has played just over 50 games for Saracens since making his debut in the 2021/22 season, having spent some time on loan at Ampthill in the Champ.

Rugby.title: Hosts South Africa and Canada crowned rugby sevens kings and queens
Rugby.summary: Hosts South Africa and Canada crowned rugby sevens kings and queens FISU
Rugby.body:
The Danie Craven stadium was buzzing with excitement as the finals of the FISU World University Championship Rugby Sevens Championship saw home team South Africa take down Uganda in a thrilling match that ended 34-7 while an emphatic Canada side beat France 20-0 in the women’s final.

Spectators from various countries filled the stands with rugby lovers, young fans and student-athletes waiting to witness who will be crowned champions in 2026. The atmosphere was filled with anticipation, and the rugby action did not disappoint.

Rugby.summary: The Newcastle Red Bulls flyer has touched down 95 times in the PREM.
Rugby.body:
Christian Wade is determined to enjoy becoming the highest try-scorer in PREM history if he eventually passes Chris Ashton, knowing it might not be long before someone comes along and knocks him off the top spot.

The Newcastle Red Bulls flyer has touched down 95 times in the PREM and is six short of Ashton’s mark, which he would likely have passed long ago but for spells in the NFL, France and Rugby League.

Rugby.title: Camborne impress in opening game in National One
Rugby.summary: Camborne are capable of taking on the top teams in National One after winning their first game since promotion, says coach Ricky Pellow.
Rugby.body:
Camborne are capable of taking on the top teams in National One after winning their first game since promotion, says coach Ricky Pellow. The Cornish side came back from 29-14 down at half time to run out 38-36 winners at Leeds Tykes to begin their campaign in the third tier with a bonus-point victory.

Ben Priddey scored two tries, while Josh Matavesi, Alex Ducker and Ben Prisk also scored as full-back Rory O'Kane scored the decisive penalty late on. "You look at the age of the squad, and there's a lot of young players in there that have played their first game for the club and also Nat One, so they're going to learn a lot," Camborne sporting director and former Exeter skills coach Pellow told BBC Radio Cornwall.

Rugby.summary: England fly-half Fin Smith has revealed the tough lesson Northampton Saints learned from their 2023/24 Gallagher PREM triumph as the champions prepare to defend the title they reclaimed last season.
Rugby.body:
England fly-half Fin Smith has revealed the tough lesson Northampton Saints learned from their 2023/24 Gallagher PREM triumph as the champions prepare to defend the title they reclaimed last season.

Despite reaching the Investec Champions Cup final in 2025, they mounted a dismal title defence, finishing in eighth place. Smith admits Saints became too consumed by trying to recreate their previous success after winning the league, with the squad repeatedly looking back at what had worked rather than finding ways to evolve.

Rugby.title: Anscombe's Scarlets debut delayed by paperwork
Rugby.summary: Scarlets hope Gareth Anscombe can debut against Dragons on Friday after a registration issue prevented him from playing against Exeter Chiefs.
Rugby.body:
Scarlets hope Gareth Anscombe can make his debut against Dragons on Friday after a registration issue prevented him from playing against Exeter Chiefs. The 35-year-old fly-half had been named to start the pre-season game at Sandy Park last weekend but was withdrawn shortly before kick-off.

Scarlets have confirmed the former Wales international was not injured and that the issue is related to his registration. The club are hopeful the paperwork will be resolved swiftly, with Anscombe set to play against Dragons at Church Bank, Llandovery on 11 September if he is cleared in time.

Rugby.summary: John Mitchell has named a 36-player WXV Global Series squad featuring 25 Women's Rugby World Cup winners.
Rugby.body:
John Mitchell has named a 36-player WXV Global Series squad featuring 25 Women’s Rugby World Cup winners. The team named for their three home fixtures in September, continues to be captained by Meg Jones in the absence of pregnant Zoe Stratford, contains three uncapped players and has a combined total of 1,234 Test caps.

All three uncapped players are forwards. Hooker pair Bryony Field and Hayley Jones will look to create competition for Amy Cokayne and May Campbell, while Gloucester Hartpury’s Sophie McQueen joins a highly competitive group of back-row players.

Rugby.summary: Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has backed Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu to be the Springboks first-choice fly-half moving forward, but has said he "needs to work through this second-year syndrome."
Rugby.body:
Former South Africa captain Victor Matfield has backed Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu to be the Springboks’ first-choice fly-half going forward, but has said he “needs to work through this second-year syndrome.”

The 24-year-old has started all three Tests of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series so far, but was originally dropped to the bench for the second Test in Cape Town before Handre Pollard, who was scheduled to start, pulled out through injury.

Rugby.title: Smaller ball for women makes it 'harder to do my job'
Rugby.summary: A smaller ball is being trialled in women's international rugby union for September and October's WXV Global Series - and it is dividing opinion.
Rugby.body:
England will play Australia, Canada and New Zealand in the next three weeks and, like all the world's top women's players, they have some new equipment: a smaller ball. During September and October's WXV Global Series, World Rugby is trialling a size 4.5 ball - about 3% smaller than the size five used in the men's game, but the same weight.

Their introduction has not been without controversy and for England hooker May Campbell, responsible for throwing the ball in at the line-out, told BBC Sport it can go "a bit skew-whiff".

Rugby.title: Mike Blair frustrated after another Test plagued by missed 'opportunities'
Rugby.summary: Blair felt that the All Blacks put the experienced Springboks players under pressure at times, but couldn't capitalise on the momentum shifts in the 80-minute contest.
Rugby.body:
Creating opportunities, but not finishing them. That’s the feeling from All Blacks assistant coach Mike Blair, who feels that at FNB Stadium, they put themselves in the right positions but couldn’t capitalise on those chances.

Blair’s admission follows the All Blacks’ 29-24 defeat to the Springboks in Soweto, where the home side were clinical in pouncing on the visitors’ mistakes. Dave Rennie’s All Blacks started the better of the two heavyweight sides, but couldn’t survive the brutal power game the Springboks threw at them.

Rugby.title: The five moments that cost the All Blacks in Soweto
Rugby.summary: The All Blacks had plenty of chances in the third Test in South Africa to claim a historic 2-1 result on South African soil.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks had plenty of chances in the third Test in South Africa to claim a historic 2-1 result on South African soil. After going up by 12-5 in the first half and 17-12 in the second half, the game was for the taking but a number of key opportunities lost didn’t build the required buffer on the scoreboard.

Dave Rennie’s side continually turn one error into a handful, leading to huge momentum swings against them. Their inability to effectively win restarts was a huge issue in this series.

Rugby.title: Wales lock Carter cleared for Dragons after injury
Rugby.summary: Dragons co-captain Ben Carter fit for start of United Rugby Championship season after recovering from ankle injury he sustained with Wales.
Rugby.body:
Dragons co-captain Ben Carter will be fit for the start of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC) after recovering from an ankle injury he sustained with Wales. The lock was ruled out of the Nations Championship defeat by South Africa in mid-July after a blow in training.

Carter, who had started Wales' six previous games, was on crutches and saw specialists on his return to Dragons. The 25-year-old did not need surgery and is working towards his side's URC opener at Benetton on Friday, 25 September (19:45 BST).

Rugby.summary: "You can't hide from it? Their set piece is pretty damn dominant, and they get a gravy train of penalties from it," Barnes admitted.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks assistant coach Neil Barnes isn’t hiding away from the Springboks’ set-piece dominance in Soweto, admitting he and scrum coach Jason Ryan have work to do. The All Blacks fell to their second straight defeat for the first time since 2024, and their second loss under new head coach Dave Rennie, who has now coached the All Blacks in six Tests and four midweek games.

Rennie’s side will look to level the four-Test series in Baltimore this weekend, as they stare down the barrel of a 3-1 series defeat at the hands of the back-to-back World Champions.

Rugby.summary: Rennie said All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea was also unlikely to feature after picking up an MCL injury in the second half.
Rugby.body:
The All Blacks have landed in Baltimore ahead of the fourth and final Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry series for 2026, but will be without nine squad members. Head coach Dave Rennie announced post-match, after their 29-24 defeat in Soweto against the Springboks, that Ardie Savea was ruled out of the Baltimore Test with a shoulder injury.

Rennie said All Blacks midfielder Quinn Tupaea was also unlikely to feature after picking up an MCL injury in the second half. After the press conferences, it was announced on social media that All Blacks vice-captain Luke Jacobson would also miss the fourth Test in Soweto with an elbow tendon issue.

Rugby.title: Rassie Erasmus on scrum battle between Boks and All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Springboks head coach has complimented the All Blacks scrum in the wake of the 29-24 win Soweto in the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series.
Rugby.body:
Springboks head coach has complimented the All Blacks scrum in the wake of the 29-24 win Soweto in the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series. After a week marred by debate of scrum tactics and fury from the Springboks fans, the scrums were in South Africa’s favour in Soweto.

The All Blacks conceded 12 penalties, many of which were at scrum time giving the Springboks an exit and territorial gain. “I think we were caught for a free kick. We were caught for collapsing one,” Erasmus said of the scrums.

Rugby.title: Uruguay star handed 13-game ban for knee-breaking tackle
Rugby.summary: Uruguayan hooker Joaquín Myszka's has been handed a 13-game ban for a red-card offence that left Chile's Emilio Shea Duret seriously injured, eight days after the incident.
Rugby.body:
Uruguayan hooker Joaquín Myszka has been handed a 13-game ban for a red-card offence that left Chile’s Emilio Shea Duret seriously injured, eight days after the incident. The incident happened in the second half of the Chile XV and Uruguay XV match for the Americas Rugby Championship, in which the Los Teros secondary team lost 33-12.

At the 52nd minute, Myszka made a low no-arms tackle to the opposing prop that resulted in a serious injury, forcing the game to be stopped for several minutes until Shea Duret was carried off the field.

Rugby.title: Itoje returns to England squad for training camp
Rugby.summary: Second row Maro Itoje returns to the England set-up after being named in a 36-man training squad for this autumn's Nations Championship matches.
Rugby.body:
Second row Maro Itoje has returned to the England set-up after being named in a 36-man training squad for this autumn's Nations Championship matches. Itoje missed matches against South Africa, Fiji and Argentina in July, taking his first proper summer break from rugby in more than a decade.

The 31-year-old, whose mother died shortly before he led England through a deflating Six Nations campaign that featured only one win, has said he has felt the benefits of his time away.

Rugby.title: Malcolm Marx is rugby's greatest bully
Rugby.summary: Then Malcolm Marx arrived his team under pressure, stooping low to dislodge the ball with a brutal...
Rugby.body:
An hour had passed in a pulsating contest in the cavernous calabash that is FNB Stadium. Minutes earlier Will Jordan had rounded a superb All Blacks move and Jesse Kriel brushed past Leroy Carter to land an instant riposte. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu’s conversion nudged the Springboks ahead for the first time. The entire series hung in the balance like a stack of Jenga tiles after one too many pieces had been removed.

Then Malcolm Marx arrived; his team under pressure, he stooped low to come up with a brutal, momentum-shifting steal. The Boks hooker shot a wagging finger and wore an expression that was less the satisfaction of a professional athlete completing a technical skill than that of a schoolyard bully mocking the unfortunate kid who had just discovered that standing up to him was a mistake.

Rugby.title: 'Nic White diving school': Cam Roigard under fire for tip tackle incident with Reinach
Rugby.summary: All Blacks halfback Cam Roigard has been accused of diving during the incident late in the first half with Cobus Reinach.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks halfback Cam Roigard has been accused of diving during the incident late in the first half where he was up ended by opposite No.9 Cobus Reinach. Roigard attempted to tackle Reinach at the base of the scrum, not aware initially that referee Nika Amushukeli had blown a penalty try.

When Roigard backed off, Reinach flipped him over aggressively with Roigard landing awkwardly. From the restart, the All Blacks were handed a penalty but no card was issued. Former Springbok midfielder Jean de Villiers made a point in commentary to call out Roigard for “gamesmanship”.

Rugby.body:
Australia coach Les Kiss insists the Wallabies will be “up for the fight” when they meet two-time defending Rugby World Cup winners the Springboks later this month, following a historic series win in Argentina.

Rugby.summary: The Wallabies have missed a chance to pinch victory against an undermanned Argentina in a 28-28 draw in Mendoza.
Rugby.body:
The Wallabies have missed a chance to pinch victory against an undermanned Argentina in a 28-28 draw in Mendoza that still secured a historic series win against Los Pumas. Chasing a fifth-straight win and fourth in a row under new coach Les Kiss, the visitors benefited from back-to-back Argentina yellow cards for deliberate knock-ons that left the hosts two short for most of the final 10 minutes.

But with Carter Gordon also off injured – halfbacks Kalani Thomas and Ryan Lonergan acted as playmakers – the hosts coughed up possession and then knocked on as Los Pumas hung on.

Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus has assessed Dave Rennie’s All Blacks after taking a 2-1 advantage in the Greatest Rivalry series, stressing that the series is not over. The hosts had the better of the first half, with scores from Paddy Pearce, Jimmy Halliwell, Gabriel Ibitoye and Noah Heward setting the tone, with Dan Robson, Ben Redshaw and Phil Cokanasiga responding for the visitors.

Rugby.title: The surprising Eben Etzebeth moment that caught Bok fans offguard
Rugby.summary: Chalk it down as 'something you don't see every day', at least not on a Test field when Eben Etzebeth is playing for the Springboks.
Rugby.body:
Chalk it down as ‘something you don’t see every day’, at least not on a Test field when Eben Etzebeth is playing for the Springboks. The Boks forwards eventually bullied New Zealand into submission in Soweto, securing a 29-24 victory and a 2-1 series lead. The All Blacks matched the Springboks’ intensity early, with Ardie Savea scoring twice before a shoulder injury ended his afternoon.

Will Jordan’s opportunistic try put New Zealand 17-12 ahead, but Jesse Kriel responded almost immediately, exposing a soft tackle and restoring South Africa’s momentum. From there, the Boks’ set-piece power took over. Malcolm Marx crashed over from a dominant maul after scrum pressure forced a penalty, while Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu’s boot stretched the lead to 12 points.

Rugby.summary: The two All Blacks left the field with injuries during the Springboks' 29-24 triumph in Soweto.
Rugby.body:
All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has provided an initial update on the health of both Ardie Savea and Quinn Tupaea. Rugby.title: South Africa finish strongly to take 2-1 series lead against All Blacks
Rugby.summary: South Africa eventually overpower a spirited New Zealand as the world champions came on strong in the final quarter in Soweto to take a 2-1 series lead.
Rugby.body:
South Africa eventually overpowered a spirited New Zealand, who could only outrun their hosts' set-piece power for so long, as the world champions came on strong in the final quarter in Soweto to take a 2-1 lead in a high-quality 'Greatest Rivalry' series.

The two sides traded two tries each in a tight first half, with New Zealand's composure and ambition with ball in hand stretching South Africa's onrushing defence. The All Blacks sniffed a famous victory when Will Jordan chased after his own kick ahead and crossed for a 17-12 lead in the 55th minute.

Rugby.summary: FNB Stadium was roaring for the third Test of the Rugby’s Greatet Rivalry series in Soweto, with 85,000 fans recognising the historic nature of the encounter between rugby’s iconic heavyweights.
Rugby.body:
FNB Stadium was roaring for the third Test of the Rugby’s Greatet Rivalry series in Soweto, with more than 85,000 fans recognising the historic nature of the encounter between rugby’s iconic heavyweights.

South Africa’s power at scrum time was a feature throughout 81 minutes of breathless rugby, and while New Zealand produced their own moments of magic, their discipline didn’t hold up in the Bok pressure-cooker. The visitors pulled ahead after a first half that was too tight to call, ultimately prevailing 29-14.

Rugby.summary: Black Ferns co-captain Georgia Ponsonby was quick to praise the Springbok Women after her team's 52-20 win at FNB Stadium.
Rugby.body:
Black Ferns co-captain Georgia Ponsonby praised the Springbok Women’s first half challenge after her team’s 52-20 win at FNB Stadium. The six-time world champions had to overcome an emboldened South Africa, who dominated at the scrum early on. Ultimately, Whitney Hansen’s Black Ferns triumphed as South African bodies tired at altitude.

Braxton Sorensen-McGee and Elinor-Plum King’s braces accounted for half of the Black Ferns’ tries, while Chryss Viliko, Maia Joseph, Ma’ama Mo’onia Vaipulu and Amarante Sititi also dotted down.

Rugby.body:
The Black Ferns overcame the Springbok Women’s pure power to register a 52-20 victory at Soweto’s FNB Stadium. In the first half, South Africa brought back a little bit of their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 magic to trail by just two points at the 20-minute mark.

Early tries for New Zealand’s Elinor-Plum King and Braxton Sorensen-McGee handed the visitors a 12-point lead. Lindelwa Gwala and Aphiwe Ngwevu hit back with a pair of tries for South Africa, who were laying down a stern challenge in close quarters.

Rugby.title: Springbok Women prove power but fall to electric Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: The first-ever Test match between the Black Ferns and Springbok Women took place at Africa's biggest stadium on Saturday afternoon, celebrating a new chapter in 'Rugby's Greatest Rivalry'.
Rugby.body:
The second-ever Test match between the Black Ferns and Springbok Women took place at Africa’s biggest stadium on Saturday afternoon, celebrating a new chapter in ‘Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry’.

The Springbok Women had their way in the scrum and won a slew of early breakdown steals, but ultimately couldn’t keep pace with the flying Kiwis, despite the women in black conceding four yellow cards. The hosts stayed within reach for the opening half, but the Black Ferns’ pace and power were too much in the end, with a winning scoreline of 52-20 registered.

Rugby.title: Portugal add former Sakura Fifteen boss to coaching staff ahead of Nations Cup
Rugby.summary: Lesley McKenzie has joined Rugby World Cup-bound Portugal after six years in charge of the Sakura Fifteen.
Rugby.body:
Lesley McKenzie has joined Rugby World Cup-bound Portugal after six years in charge of the Sakura Fifteen. The 25-cap Canada international has joined Simon Mannix’s Portugal coaching staff as a contact coach focusing on the breakdown, winning collisions and tackle technique. In November, Os Lobos will play World Rugby Nations Cup fixtures against Chile, Samoa and Uruguay in Lisbon.

At Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025, McKenzie’s Japan exited the tournament after a third-place finish in Pool C before concluding their time in England with a 29-21 victory against Spain in York.

Rugby.summary: Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter says that the chances of Wallaby superstar Len Ikitau returning to Sandy Park after the 2027 World Cup in Australia are hanging in the balance.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter says that the chances of Wallaby superstar Len Ikitau returning to Sandy Park after the 2027 World Cup in Australia are hanging in the balance. Outside centre Ikitau spent last season in Devon, making 13 appearances and scoring four tries, but Baxter brought in Will Butt from Bath, while Dallas McLeod will arrive at the club following the NPC.

“We had some very early discussions, but it’s probably too early to say any more than that. We brought in Dallas, and we’ll see how our young players go, because that may have sealed off the squad for Len,” he said.

Rugby.title: The former England U18 star thriving after taking a chance in New Zealand
Rugby.summary: Worboys scored 23 points, kicking nine goals from nine attempts: five penalties and four conversions, as Manawatu snapped North Harbour’s three-game winning streak.
Rugby.body:
George Worboys has found an unlikely rugby home in Palmerston North. The former England Under-18 first five, who passed through the prestigious Bath Rugby Academy and played in the senior team with the British and Irish Lions ten Finn Russell, is thriving for Manawatu in the NPC.

After making a big impact from the bench in Manawatu’s improbable 36-35 comeback win against Southland on August 8, he started the next three games. On Saturday, Worboys scored 23 points, kicking nine goals from nine attempts: five penalties and four conversions, as Manawatu snapped North Harbour’s three-game winning streak 43-40.

The injury rumours that circulated in the media earlier in the week about Carter Gordon have proven to be incorrect, but that doesn’t erase the discourse that followed the reporting.

Gordon has had an injury-riddled return to rugby since his stint in the NRL, and it has put a strain on the Wallaby playmaking stocks. It’s clear that there is no preferred or trusted back-up to Gordon currently in the Wallabies squad, and coach Les Kiss cannot afford to be sentimental; he must deal with the issue at hand.

Rugby.summary: When it comes to global sports, few things get bums on seats more than a celebrity star player signing.
Rugby.body:
When it comes to global sports, few things get bums on seats more than a celebrity star player signing. While in the past, rugby has been slower to the table compared to the likes of football when it comes to leaning to that star power, the last few years has seen that change, the likes of France’s Antoine Dupont and the USA’s Ilona Maher commanding significant profiles.

Showing athletes not just for their skill on the field, but their personality off it has become a primary goal for the inaugural season of the Ultimate Sevens, the competition sparing no expense in getting some of the biggest names in the short format of the game.

Rugby.title: Kolisi urges Boks to channel spirit of Soweto to beat All Blacks
Rugby.summary: Captain Siya Kolisi calls on the Springboks to summon inspiration from Soweto's pivotal part in South Africa's history as they host New Zealand on Saturday.
Rugby.body:
Captain Siya Kolisi has called on the Springboks to summon inspiration from Soweto's pivotal part in South Africa's history as they take on New Zealand on the edge of the Johannesburg township on Saturday.

The 94,736-capacity FNB Stadium staged the opening match of football's World Cup, the first and only time the tournament has been staged in Africa. However, Kolisi, South Africa's first black captain, also referenced 1976's Soweto Uprising - the student protests that were a turning point in the fight against apartheid, the state-backed racial segregation of South African society.

Rugby.summary: There is exactly one year to go until the British & Irish Lions Women play their first tour match in New Zealand.
Rugby.body:
There is exactly one year to go until the British & Irish Lions Women play their first tour match in New Zealand. By then the British & Irish Lions Women will have been a project more than six years in the making. Now it is 12 months away from becoming a reality.

It is a team that was launched after a feasibility study that took just shy of three years before it was announced a team would come into existence, and give the top players from England, Ireland, Scotland and Wales the opportunity to compete together under one banner for the very first time. A game changer for women’s rugby.

Rugby.title: 'I’m not one to keep secrets': Swys de Bruin lifts the lid on his abrupt Springbok Women exit
Rugby.summary: Swys de Bruin has opened up about his abrupt departure as head coach of the Springbok Women.
Rugby.body:
Swys de Bruin has opened up about his shock exit as head coach of the Springbok Women. This week, ahead of the team’s Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry clash with the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium, rumours emerged that De Bruin had resigned.

Later, when the Boks announced their match day 23 for the Soweto fixture, SA Rugby confirmed that the 66-year-old had left his post. During his two years in charge – which De Bruin described as “wonderful” – the former Lions and Springbok Men attack coach led his team to the knockout stages of a Women’s Rugby World Cup for the first time ever.

Rugby.title: The emergence of softly-spoken Peter Lakai within the All Blacks environment
Rugby.summary: Quiet characters are easy to find in the All Blacks environment, far more so than outspoken ones. But even by New Zealand's standards, Peter Lakai stands out as especially laid-back and undisturbed.
Rugby.body:
Quiet characters are easy to find in the All Blacks environment, far more so than outspoken ones. But even by New Zealand standards, Peter Lakai stands out as especially laid-back and undisturbed.

The 23-year-old is in his third season with the national team, having generated All Blacks buzz with his New Zealand Age Grade Player of the Year Award in 2022 after debuting and starring for the Wellington Lions as a teenager. Lakai has since established himself as a non-negotiable selection in the All Blacks’ matchday 23, thanks in large part to his remarkable consistency for such a young athlete.

Rugby.title: New family dynasty set for special piece of Test history in Soweto
Rugby.summary: The Sititi family will take centre stage at FNB Stadium on Saturday, with 19-year-old sensation Amarante named for the Black Ferns and 23-year-old brother Wallace named for the All Blacks in the Greatest Rivalry double-header.
Rugby.body:
The Sititi family will take centre stage at FNB Stadium on Saturday, with 19-year-old sensation Amarante named for the Black Ferns and 23-year-old brother Wallace named for the All Blacks in the Greatest Rivalry double-header.

It’s just the second time siblings have represented New Zealand on the same day, following Annaleah and Xavier Rush in 1998. Both siblings have been named in the No.20 jerseys for their respective teams, with Amarante set to make just her second Test appearance for the Black Ferns and Wallace in line to make his 22nd Test appearance for the All Blacks.

Rugby.summary: Springboks captain Siya Kolisi has stated his desire for supporters to flock to FNB Stadium for the Springbok Women's match with the Black Ferns.
Rugby.body:
Springboks captain Siya Kolisi has urged supporters to flock to FNB Stadium for the Springbok Women’s match with the Black Ferns. This weekend, South Africa’s biggest stadium will see the Springbok Women and the six-time world champion Black Ferns go toe-to-toe for just the third time. Ever. The fixture will also be the curtain-raiser to the third Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

To date, the Springbok Women and Black Ferns have played each other just twice. The last of those encounters came just shy of a year ago in a Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-final in Exeter.
Rugby.copy:
Springboks captain Siya Kolisi has urged supporters to flock to FNB Stadium for the Springbok Women’s match with the Black Ferns. This weekend, South Africa’s biggest stadium will see the Springbok Women and the six-time world champion Black Ferns go toe-to-toe for just the third time. Ever. The fixture will also be the curtain-raiser to the third Test of Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

To date, the Springbok Women and Black Ferns have played each other just twice. The last of those encounters came just shy of a year ago in a Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-final in Exeter.

Rugby.title: Nationwide Nadi Rugby Sevens
Rugby.summary: Nationwide Nadi Rugby Sevens Manly Observer
Rugby.body:
On 24–25 October 2026, the Nationwide Nadi Rugby 7’s will take over Pittwater Rugby Park in Warriewood, bringing a major celebration of Pacific rugby, culture and community to the Northern Beaches.

The two-day tournament will feature a 32-team men’s Rugby Sevens competition together with a women’s competition, attracting players, officials, families and supporters for a weekend of fast-paced rugby.

Rugby.title: Singleton hopes for rugby union return after heart attack
Rugby.summary: Jack Singleton hopes to return to rugby union and is looking for a new club, a year after suffering a heart attack.
Rugby.body:
A year after suffering a heart attack, hooker Jack Singleton is hoping to return to full training next month to get his rugby union career back on track. Singleton had played one Prem Cup game for Gloucester in September 2025, as the 2025-26 campaign was getting under way, when he had the heart attack aged 29 while training at the club.

"We're not really sure when it started but it wasn't like a scary moment for me, it was just a lot of symptoms or dizziness [and an] aching arm," he told BBC Radio Gloucestershire.

Rugby.title: Club legend emerges as favourite to replace Leo Cullen at Leinster
Rugby.summary: Cullen has been in charge of Leinster since 2015.
Rugby.body:
Felipe Contepomi has emerged as the favourite to make a romantic return to Leinster to replace Leo Cullen when he stands down at the end of the season. Argentina’s all-time leading points scorer, Contepomi, 49, is regarded as one of Leinster’s club legends after spending six years at the RDS as a player and a further four on the coaching staff before leaving in 2023 to return to Argentina.

He first served as an assistant to Michael Cheika at the 2023 World Cup, then took over the top job, and now Leinster, who have drawn up a shortlist he heads, will have to try to tempt him away.

Rugby.title: Rankings: What a win in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry could mean for the Springbok Women
Rugby.summary: The Springbok Women could leap three places up the World Rugby rankings with a shock win against the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium.
Rugby.body:
The Springbok Women could leap three places up the World Rugby rankings with a shock win against the Black Ferns at FNB Stadium. On Saturday, the Springbok Women and Black Ferns will play one another as part of a doubleheader in Soweto. The fixture acts as a curtain-raiser to the Springboks and All Blacks‘ third Test in Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry.

Any victory for the Springbok Women will see them move three places up the World Rugby rankings from 10th to seventh. An additional place is up for grabs if South Africa win by 15 points or more.

Rugby.title: 'They don't play hide and seek': Springboks react to All Blacks' selection tweaks
Rugby.summary: The Springboks say the All Blacks have sent a message with their selections for the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series, and that message has been received loud and clear.
Rugby.body:
The Springboks say the All Blacks have sent a message with their selections for the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series, and that message has been received loud and clear.

New Zealand selectors have turned to some fresh bodies for the must-win Soweto Test, knowing a loss this week would eliminate their chances of a series win. The tweaks have all come in the forward pack, where Asafo Aumua, Sam Darry and Peter Lakai have been injected into the starting lineup at the expense of Codie Taylor, Simon Parker and Fabian Holland, although the latter has remained in the matchday 23.

Rugby.title: What Rob Baxter wants to see from Tommy Wyatt's long-awaited comeback
Rugby.summary: Wyatt, 26, who can play in any of the back-five positions, last played for the Chiefs in a home defeat to Sale Sharks in May 2025.
Rugby.body:
Exeter Chiefs boss Rob Baxter wants to see full-back Tommy Wyatt play with a smile on his face when he makes his long-awaited comeback on Saturday. Wyatt is set to end his two-year injury hell after being named on the bench for the friendly at Sandy Park.

The 26-year-old, who can play in any of the back-five positions, last played for the Chiefs in a home defeat to Sale Sharks in May 2025. He damaged ligaments to his right knee early in 2024 in a game against Glasgow and then suffered the same fate to his left knee in the final game of the 2024/25 season, which led to him missing the whole of last year’s campaign.

Rugby.body:
The Gallagher PREM Cup gets underway this weekend with some teams using the competition primarily as a development tool for academy and fringe players and others as first-team prep for when the league season begins later this month.

Rugby.summary: The Oranje Dames XV have named the squad that will compete in the WXV Global Series Challenger this month.
Rugby.body:
The Oranje Dames XV have named the squad that will compete in the WXV Global Series Challenger this month. The Netherlands prepared for their trip to Hong Kong China with a 33-0 win over a Scotland A team coached by Claire Cruikshank.

Linde van der Velden scored a brace in Amsterdam, while Mariet Luijken and Esmee Ligtvoet were also try scorers last Saturday. It was the final home fixture for the team’s head coach, Gareth Gilbert, who will return to his native South Africa after the WXV Global Series Challenger.
