Rugby.title: ‘Pre-season seems to contain a mind-altering opiate that erases all ills from the past season and floods the brain with enriching optimism’
Rugby.summary: With no annoying league table to offer a crushing reality check, a swirling world of possibilities await every club for the campaign ahead.
Rugby.body:
The start of the English rugby season may have been put back by a fortnight for the rank and file because of the summer heatwave and its effect on the playing surfaces up and down the country, but the top end will get under way this weekend with the Prem Cup.

To be honest the Prem Cup is more of a tip-toe than a leap into the new season even if Bristol v Gloucester on Saturday will be televised on TNT Sports. The competition is a pale imitation of the domestic cup whose final used to fill Twickenham in its glory days.

Rugby.summary: Frenchman Belleau is one of 10 players unavailable for the clash at the StoneX Stadium.
Rugby.body:
With England star Fin Smith enjoying a mandatory rest period and Anthony Belleau picking up an unspecified training ground injury, Northampton have handed 18-year-old fly-half Hugh Shields his senior debut this Saturday.

The England U18 international and son of former Saints hooker and current first-team manager Paul Shields, starts the season’s opener against Saracens in the Gallagher PREM Rugby Cup and is one of seven potential debutants.

Rugby.summary: As Yaras head coach Guilherme Coghetto has confirmed his squad that will travel to Hong Kong China for the WXV Global Series Challenger.
Rugby.body:
As Yaras head coach Guilherme Coghetto has confirmed his squad that will travel to Hong Kong China for the WXV Global Series Challenger. The former assistant coach has included 11 players with Olympic Games experience, as well as 16 players who represented Brazil at last year’s Women’s Rugby World Cup in England.

Across three weeks, Brazil will play fixtures against Hong Kong China, the Netherlands and Spain. It will be the first time ever that As Yaras have played Hong Kong China, while they have taken on the Netherlands five times previously and Las Leonas once.

Rugby.summary: Cardiff head coach Corniel van Zyl says Taulupe Faletau has returned to non-contact training and thinks he will still want to play for Wales.
Rugby.body:
Cardiff are hopeful that Wales number eight Taulupe Faletau will be fit for the start of the 2026-27 United Rugby Championship (URC). The 35-year-old suffered a season-ending shoulder injury at Sharks in March, and was limited to just seven appearances in the past campaign after knee and calf issues earlier in the campaign.

Faletau has featured in pre-season training and will soon step up his comeback in the build-up to the URC opener against Scarlets on Saturday, 26 September (19:45 BST). Head coach Corniel van Zyl said: "Even though he can't do contact, he can still run so fitness-wise he's in a good space.

Rugby.title: Scarlets release new prop Apoua after torn Achilles
Rugby.summary: Scarlets suffer blow before new United Rugby Championship season with the loss of summer signing Chris Apoua to an Achilles injury.
Rugby.body:
Scarlets have released summer signing Chris Apoua after the forward ruptured an Achilles in training. The 34-year-old tight-head prop signed for the Llanelli-based club in August from Super Rugby side Moana Pasifika.

But the veteran, who has played provincial rugby in New Zealand with Northland and Southland, suffered a serious injury soon after linking up with Nigel Davies' squad and will miss the entire 2026-27 season.

Rugby.title: All Blacks prop George Bower has message for the Bok scrum
Rugby.summary: All Blacks loosehead George Bower has made it clear he does not fear packing down against the Springboks in the third Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry test in Soweto...
Rugby.body:
All Blacks loosehead George Bower has made it clear he does not fear packing down against the Springboks in the third Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry test in Soweto and is relishing another head-to-head that could have a major bearing on the result.

With the series tied 1-1 after the Springboks won the second test after losing the opener, the scrum has become the focal point for both coaches after All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie accused the Boks of walking around the scrum. Opposite number Rassie Erasmus responded strongly in defence of his players and all week the home side has dismissed the All Blacks attacks.

Rugby.summary: Japan head coach Eddie Jones has made five changes to the starting XV that crashed to a 56-17 defeat to Australia three weeks ago for Saturday's Centenary Test against Canada in Niigata City.
Rugby.body:
Japan head coach Eddie Jones has made five changes to the starting XV that crashed to a 56-17 defeat to Australia three weeks ago for Saturday’s Centenary Test against Canada in Niigata City.

Notably, captain and lock Warner Dearns is out as one of three changes to the pack, with Jack Cornelsen named as Harry Hockings’ partner in the second row. Scrum-half Naoto Saito takes on the armband in the absence of Dearns. Saito has captained the Brave Blossoms twice before, against Uruguay and England in 2024.

Rugby.title: Danelle Lochner: 'We’re a much better team than the one that lost last year'
Rugby.summary: For 15 minutes between the two halves of their Women's Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-final against New Zealand, South Africa were in dreamland.
Rugby.body:
For 15 minutes between the two halves of their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-final against New Zealand, South Africa were in dreamland. A side that had never been in the knockouts of the game’s premier competition were all square at 10-10 with the team who had lifted the trophy more than any other. But South Africa weren’t hanging on.

They had dominated the opening 40 minutes against the Black Ferns, scoring two tries through rumbling forward play and dynamic running off the shoulder and around the corner. The maul was thrumming. The breakdown was immense. If anything, they deserved a lead.

Rugby.body:
Ben Carter and Angus O’Brien have been named Dragons RFC co-captains for the 2026/27 season – the Newport-Gwent-based URC outfit has confirmed. The pair will share the role for a third consecutive campaign, having led the Welsh region in the United Rugby Championship and EPCR Challenge Cup over the past two seasons.

They will be supported by Harrison Keddie, Aneurin Owen, Matthew Screech and Thomas Young, who form part of the club’s senior leadership group. Head Coach Filo Tiatia said: “I’m delighted to confirm Ben and Angus will continue to lead us into the new season.

Rugby.title: Why Caluori played on with detached wrist ligament
Rugby.summary: Wing sensation Noah Caluori says he played through the pain of a torn wrist ligament during his break-out season for Saracens and England
Rugby.body:
Teenage wing sensation Noah Caluori has revealed that he spent the majority of his breakthrough season - featuring 18 tries in 13 Prem games and an England debut - playing with a detached ligament in his wrist.

The 19-year-old sustained the injury when he came down heavily on his arm while competing for a high ball in Saracens' defeat by Exeter in December. After consulting both club and national team coaches, Caluori opted to play through his pain and wait until the summer for an operation to reconnect the ligament.

Rugby.summary: Ben Donaldson hasn’t started a Wallabies match at fly-half in practically two years to the day, but the 24-Test utility will get that opportunity this weekend.
Rugby.body:
Ben Donaldson hasn’t started a Wallabies match at fly-half in practically two years to the day, but the 24-Test utility will get that opportunity this weekend after swamping spots with Carter Gordon.

Gordon wore the No. 10 jersey in wins over Japan’s Brave Blossoms in Townsville and Los Pumas at Jujuy’s Estadio 23 de Agosto, but the Queenslander has shifted to the bench for the second match in South America.

Rugby.summary: USA U20s captain Spencer Huntley is no stranger to being the youngest rugby prospect in the room.
Rugby.body:
USA U20s captain Spencer Huntley is no stranger to being the youngest rugby prospect in the room. It’s a challenge the scrum-half became quite accustomed to throughout the age-grade ranks, before being named in an Eagles-heavy USA XV squad last month.

Huntley first got the chance to play for the USA U20s as a 17-year-old, before suiting up for the U23s at just 18. These weren’t opportunities Huntley was daunted by, with the teenager working hard to show “there’s a reason why I’m here.”

Rugby.body:
Beno Obano will become the latest England player to put his Test career on ice with a move to France, after agreeing to join Top 14 side Pau from Bath at the end of the forthcoming season.

The 31-year-old loose-head prop won his fifth cap in the defeat by South Africa in July, backing up first-choice Ellis Genge off the bench. Head coach Steve Borthwick is restricted to a domestic-based talent pool as a key part of the relationship between Prem clubs and the Rugby Football Union over elite players.

Rugby.summary: Defending Super Rugby Pacific champions the Hurricanes have added an All Blacks XV forward to their roster.
Rugby.body:
Defending Super Rugby Pacific champions the Hurricanes have added an All Blacks XV forward to their roster ahead of the 2027 season, with Oliver Haig making the move to the capital after a stint down south with the Highlanders.

Haig started at blindside flanker for the All Blacks XV in a 38-24 win over Irish club side Munster in late 2024, and the utility forward also spent time with the All Blacks as injury cover ahead of a Test away to Japan’s Brave Blossoms.

Rugby.title: Len Ikitau returns as Wallabies shake up starting side for Los Pumas
Rugby.summary: Len Ikitau hasn’t played for the Wallabies since July 18, but the reigning John Eales Medal winner will make his long-awaited return to the Test arena.
Rugby.body:
Len Ikitau hasn’t played for the Wallabies since July 18, but the reigning John Eales Medal winner will make his long-awaited return to the Test arena after being named to start alongside Joseph-Aukuso Suaalii against Los Pumas in Mendoza.

Ikitau missed both Flight Centre Series matches against the Brave Blossoms due to injury, with Hunter Paisami instead stringing a series of starts together. But Paisami has been rotated out of the matchday 23 this week, with Ikitau set for his 54th Wallabies appearance.

Rugby.title: 'It's funny, our game': Dave Rennie bows out of Springboks scrum saga
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie has started to wind down the scrum chat ahead of the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry tour, attempting to move on from what has become a contentious talking point in the series.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie has started to wind down the scrum chat ahead of the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry tour, attempting to move on from what has become a contentious talking point in the series.

The All Blacks coach kicked off the saga by calling out South Africa for walking around in the scrum, prompting an impassioned rebuttal from counterpart Rassie Erasmus. Former players, podcasters, pundits and columnists have feasted on the topic since, amplifying the sense of tension in the series from afar.

Biarritz has always known how to host rugby in a unique way. Here, the oval ball doesn’t just fill a stadium—it’s part of the landscape, just like the waves and the terraces that are still packed in September. It’s only natural that this seaside town was chosen as the third stop onthe Ultimate Sevens tour, the new rugby sevens tournament. Forget the 80-minute games and the never-ending halftime break. Ultimate Sevens packs it all in: matches lasting about ten minutes, with no breaks, so the action never stops. The tournament follows a highly dynamic single-elimination format, where every match is decisive.

Rugby.title: ‘Expect the unexpected’: Whitney Hansen delivers warning to Black Ferns ahead of Boks clash
Rugby.summary: Whitney Hansen has told her Black Ferns team to "expect the unexpected" against the Springbok Women at FNB Stadium this weekend.
Rugby.body:
Whitney Hansen has told her Black Ferns team to “expect the unexpected” against the Springbok Women at FNB Stadium this weekend. It will be the first time that the two teams have played one another on South African soil, with the fixture forming part of a Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry doubleheader ahead of the Springboks men’s third Test against the All Blacks.

The last time the two teams met was in a Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 quarter-final at Exeter’s Sandy Park, where the Black Ferns won 46-27 after the scoreboard read 10-10 at the halfway point.

Rugby.title: ‘Right squad for this game’: Springbok Women bank on experience against Black Ferns
Rugby.summary: The Springbok Women have lent on experience for their Women's Rugby World Cup quarter-final repeat with the Black Ferns this weekend in Soweto.
Rugby.body:
The Springbok Women have lent on experience for their Women’s Rugby World Cup quarter-final repeat with the Black Ferns this weekend in Soweto. In total, 11 of the starting XV that took on the Black Ferns in their Women’s Rugby World Cup 2025 meeting last year will start Saturday’s clash, which forms part of a Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry doubleheader at FNB Stadium.

It was announced at the squad announcement that South Africa head coach Swys de Bruin had left his role. As a result, assistant coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September will lead the team as co-coaches.

Rugby.title: Dave Rennie explains big Codie Taylor call and other All Blacks changes for Soweto
Rugby.summary: Dave Rennie has explained the changes he and his selectors have made to the All Blacks' matchday 23 for the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series in Soweto.
Rugby.body:
Dave Rennie has explained the changes he and his selectors have made to the All Blacks‘ matchday 23 for the third Test of the Greatest Rivalry series in Soweto. The coach opted to tinker with his forward pack and leave his backline intact for the pivotal match, with Asafo Aumua, Sam Darry and Peter Lakai the big winners of the rethink.

Aumua takes Codie Taylor’s place in the starting XV after some impressive performances off the bench to begin the 2026 Test season, and will be backed up by Samisoni Taukei’aho, who will play his first minutes of the Test series off the bench.

Rugby.title: Jake White: What people are reliably getting wrong about the scrum
Rugby.summary: Scrum debate: I’ll tell you a story. One that may give you context to the events of the past few days.
Rugby.body:
I’ll tell you a story. One that may give you context to the events of the past few days. In the famous 1949 New Zealand tour of South Africa – the one in which the Springboks whitewashed the All Blacks 4-0 – Danie ‘Doc’ Craven was the South Africa coach.

Back then, it took the tourists 26-days to travel by boat to South Africa, and even then, more boat travel was required to move from Test to Test. Legend has it that on one voyage, ‘Doc’ Craven, boarded the ship and assisted the travelling opponents in the art of scrummaging. Whether it was true or not is open to conjecture, but the story has grown legs over the last 77 years and is a parable about the foundations of the The Greatest Rivalry. Either way, what cannot be disputed is Doc’s authority as a visionary coach and man of outstanding virtue. Indeed, he played and captained the Springboks pre-war. He coached Stellenbosch and the Springboks for seven years and as an administrator was SARU President and IRB (World Rugby) Chairman, all while being a noted author on rugby strategy and tactics. He did it all.

Rugby.title: Statement: SA Rugby confirm the future of Springbok Women boss Swys de Bruin
Rugby.summary: SA Rugby have confirmed that Swys de Bruin has stepped away as head coach of the Springbok Women two days before their Rugby's Greatest Rivalry match with the Black Ferns.
Rugby.body:
SA Rugby have confirmed that Swys de Bruin has stepped away as head coach of the Springbok Women two days before their Rugby’s Greatest Rivalry match with the Black Ferns. In the interim, assistant coaches Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September have been announced as co-head coaches. The pair have led South Africa to title success at this year’s Rugby Africa Women’s Cup in Kenya, and in their tour whitewash of the Fijiana XV.

SA Rugby, in their squad announcement, said: “Media are advised that Laurian Johannes-Haupt and Franzel September, who led the team to success in Kenya and Fiji earlier this year, will continue to act as co-head coaches of the Springbok Women’s team following the decision by Swys de Bruin to step down from the role. No further comment will be made in the short-term to allow the team to focus on their match with New Zealand’s Black Ferns.”

Rugby.summary: Centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg admits he "probably would have loved to" play for his native South Africa, but denies Rassie Erasmus' claims he was in talks over a Springboks call-up.
Rugby.body:
Centre Benhard Janse van Rensburg has admitted that he "probably would have loved to" play for his native South Africa, but denied Rassie Erasmus' claim he was in talks over a Springboks call-up before making his England debut.

Janse van Rensburg, who represented South Africa's under-20 side, became eligible for England this summer after living in the country for five years and scored on his Test bow against Fiji in Liverpool in July.

Rugby.title: Decision imminent on in-demand Ronan O'Gara's future
Rugby.summary: Ronan O'Gara is in talks with La Rochelle about extending his deal with the club until 2031, French outlet Sud Ouest have reported.
Rugby.body:
Ronan O’Gara is in talks with La Rochelle about extending his deal with the club until 2031, French outlet Sud Ouest have reported. The Irishman is heading into his eighth season with La Rochelle, his sixth at the helm, but is entering the final year of his contract.

La Rochelle’s slump in recent seasons has invited plenty of speculation over whether the 49-year-old would leave the Atlantic coast at the end of the season, or even whether he would see out his contract.

Rugby.title: Why the smart money should be on rugby sevens
Rugby.summary: Why the smart money should be on rugby sevens City AM
Rugby.body:
Why should we be taking more notice of rugby sevens at the moment, asks former player Jim Hamilton. There are different versions of rugby, and while the 15-a-side game will always be my Everest, sevens offers something completely different. The sport is simple to follow, fast and incredibly athletic, and it allows individual personalities and athletes to shine in a way that can be harder in 15s. But the opportunity of rugby sevens goes well beyond what happens on the pitch.

Sevens has always had the travel, entertainment and experience built into it from the start – Hong Kong and Cape Town come to mind as great destinations. Anyone who has been to either of those tournaments understands that you are not simply getting a ticket to watch rugby but buying into a weekend and a host city.

Tennis.title: GB's Salisbury & Ram beat champions to reach semis
Tennis.summary: Three-time US Open doubles champions Joe Salisbury and Rajeev Ram beat last year's winners Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos to reach the semi-finals.
Tennis.body:
Reunited three-time US Open men's doubles champions Joe Salisbury and Rajeev Ram knocked out last year's winners Marcel Granollers and Horacio Zeballos to reach the semi-finals.

Britain's Salisbury won the title at at Flushing Meadows in New York alongside American Ram in 2021, 2022 and 2023, but they split in 2024 before teaming up again this year. They won 6-4 6-4 against the second seeds and will face 2024 runners-up Kevin Krawietz and Tim Putz from Germany on Thursday.

Tennis.title: Zverev storms into semi-finals despite late bedtime
Tennis.summary: Alexander Zverev storms into the US Open last four despite staying up until 3:30am to watch Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz's blockbuster quarter-final.
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev booked his place in the US Open semi-finals with a commanding victory over Botic van de Zandschulp - despite staying up until 3:30am to watch Ben Shelton and Carlos Alcaraz's blockbuster quarter-final.

The top seed swept aside the Dutchman with a 6-2 7-5 6-1 win in the night session on Arthur Ashe Stadium. Following his victory, Zverev revealed he had stayed up to watch Shelton's win over defending champion Alcaraz in a match that ended at 03:34 local time on Wednesday - the latest finish in the tournament's history.

Tennis.title: US Open: Alexander Zverev passes Botic van de ​Zandschulp test to set up semi-final date with Karen Khachanov
Tennis.summary: US Open: Alexander Zverev passes Botic van de ​Zandschulp test to set up semi-final date with Karen Khachanov Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Alexander Zverev took another big step towards a second Grand Slam title by beating Dutchman Botic van de Zandschulp 6-2 7-5 6-1 to reach the US Open semi-finals. The 29-year-old French Open champion and Wimbledon runner-up got off to a slow start in his campaign at Flushing Meadows but has steadily found his range.

Zverev played five-set matches in each of the first two matches, but he has won his last three in straight sets and is the only man to reach all four Grand Slam semi-finals this year.

Tennis.title: US Open: Top-seeded quartet set for women's semi-final showdown with Aryna Sabalenka and Coco Gauff in action
Tennis.summary: US Open: Top-seeded quartet set for women's semi-final showdown with Aryna Sabalenka and Coco Gauff in action Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka will bid to move one step closer to a third straight US Open title when she faces familiar foe Jessica Pegula, while Elena Rybakina will take on home favourite Coco Gauff in the semi-finals on Thursday from midnight - live on Sky Sports Tennis.

For the first time since Wimbledon in 2009, all four top seeds at a Grand Slam have reached the semi-finals, with Sabalenka, Rybakina and Gauff all former major champions and third seed Pegula seeking a maiden Grand Slam title.

Tennis.title: 'Warrior' Gauff saves match points to set up Rybakina semi-final
Tennis.summary: Coco Gauff saves two match points to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up a US Open semi-final against incoming world number one Elena Rybakina.
Tennis.body:
Coco Gauff saved two match points as she fought from a set down to beat Mirra Andreeva and set up a US Open semi-final against incoming world number one Elena Rybakina. Blown away in a 26-minute opening set, fourth seed Gauff was twice pegged back from a break up in a scrappy second set before coming through a 16-point tie-break to force a decider.

Roared on by a partisan crowd, the American's resilience proved the difference in what became a mental battle as she closed out a 2-6 7-6 (9-7) 6-2 win – a performance she said was inspired by compatriot Frances Tiafoe's comeback victory over Alex Michelsen on Tuesday night.

Tennis.title: Hewett and Reid into last eight of US Open singles
Tennis.summary: British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid win their respective first-round matches in the men's wheelchair singles at the US Open.
Tennis.body:
British duo Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid both reached the men's wheelchair singles quarter-finals at the US Open on Wednesday. Hewett, the number two seed and a four-time winner in New York, dropped only two games in a 6-0 6-2 victory against Spain's Daniel Caverzaschi and will face American Casey Ratzlaff for a place in the semi-finals.

Reid's match against Frenchman Stephane Houdet was a much closer contest, with the Scot eventually winning 6-3 5-7 6-2 in two hours and 13 minutes. Up next for Reid is the defending champion and top seed Tokito Oda of Japan, who has won the past six Grand Slam singles titles.

Tennis.title: US Open: 3.33am local time and another early-morning finish as Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz, so does something have to change?
Tennis.summary: US Open: 3.33am local time and another early-morning finish as Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz, so does something have to change? Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
US Open: 3.33am local time and another early-morning finish as Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz, so does something have to change? The clock ticked to 3.33am local time in New York City when Ben Shelton beat Carlos Alcaraz with a clean ace to the delight of thousands of delirious tennis fans still inside Arthur Ashe Stadium, but does something have to be done to stop these early-morning finishes?

Three long matches earlier on Tuesday meant Alcaraz and Shelton did not step on to court until gone 11pm. The US Open craves its night matches and players love the energy the fans provide - even when a number of matches have already gone past 2am this year.

Coco Gauff saved two match points on her way to a three-set victory over teenage French Open winner Mirra Andreeva which set up a semi-final showdown with newly crowned world No 1 Elena Rybakina.

Tennis.title: 'Just a number'
Tennis.summary: Elena Rybakina becomes the new women's world number one after reaching the US Open semi-finals, ending Aryna Sabalenka's 99-week reign at the top of the rankings.
Tennis.body:
After 99 weeks, there will be a new women's world number one - and it will be Elena Rybakina. Rybakina confirmed she will replace Aryna Sabalenka at the top of the world rankings on Monday with her US Open quarter-final victory over China's Zheng Qinwen.

Despite losing a set for the first time in the tournament, Rybakina fought back and saved a break point in the deciding set to complete a 3-6 6-1 6-4 win. She is the first Kazakhstani man or woman to reach the top of the singles standings.

Coco had a difficult start of this match , with a lot of unforced errors and not feeling at her best . Mirra Andreeva has been clinical in capitalizing all her opportunities to run away with the 1st set . However we are sure Coco is going to try her absolute best to find solutions and stop all those unforced errors from her forehand side as well as the double faults .

Gauff cannot build any momentum from going 0-15 up, firing the next point into the net and the next two wide. And, after a promising start, a familiar story of Gauff errors unfold as she fires long looking to force the issue.

Tennis.title: Who Is Emma Raducanu's New Boyfriend? The Romance Explained
Tennis.summary: Who Is Emma Raducanu's New Boyfriend? The Romance Explained Grazia Daily UK
Tennis.body:
The US Open is fully underway, and tennis fans will notice that one star player is noticeably missing: Emma Raducanu. It’s a tournament that has special significance for the British player. Five years ago, a then 18-year-old Raducanu dazzled the tennis world by becoming the first and only qualifier to win the US Open, securing the women’s singles title.

This year, we won't be seeing the tennis star on the court. Due to a stress fracture in her shin, which also saw her drop out of Wimbledon, Raducanu is unable to play in this year’s US Open.

Tennis.title: Shelton beats Alcaraz in latest-ever US Open finish to reach semis
Tennis.summary: Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defence is over after a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton which ends at 03:34 local time.
Tennis.body:
Carlos Alcaraz's US Open title defence came to an end in a dramatic five-set quarter-final loss to Ben Shelton which ended at 03:34 local time - the latest finish in the tournament's history.

A large crowd remained captivated deep into the night as a modern classic unfolded over an unpredictable four hours and 28 minutes on Arthur Ashe Stadium. The match did not begin until about 11pm in New York, after the start of the night session was delayed by Tuesday's earlier matches.

Tennis.title: Osaka makes passionate defence of on-court outfits
Tennis.summary: Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path".
Tennis.body:
Naomi Osaka says any criticism she receives for her extravagant outfits is "worth it" if it means "the people after me have an easier path". The 28-year-old is renowned for her eye-catching on-court attire, which included a hooded white gown for her first-round win against Anastasia Zakharova at the US Open.

Underneath was an all-black basketball-style kit in which Osaka played, while she also had her hair braided and wore a headband in a tribute to former NBA star Allen Iverson, who she called a "trailblazer" as "he's kind of like done a lot in fashion, whether it's on purpose or not".

Tennis.title: More than the Score
Tennis.summary: Crowd behaviour has been in the spotlight at the US Open
Tennis.body: This year, the US Open gave accreditation to nearly 100 social media influencers and content creators. The tournament sees them as crucial to helping promote tennis to younger audiences - but they've also been accused of disrupting matches. Jessica Pegula and Naomi Osaka are among the players who have complained about crowd behaviour at Flushing Meadows, with umpires having to pause some matches due to excess noise and bright lights in the stands. But do influencers deserve this criticism - and what are content creators and tennis gaining from each other? Rachel Stuhlmann, one of the world's leading tennis influencers, tells More than the Score's Delyth Lloyd how she's built her career over the past decade, and the day-to-day realities of creating content at the world's biggest tournaments. Delyth's also joined by Sara Gordano from the sports business site Sportico, who explains tennis's relationship with the creator economy - and why the US Open's "party" atmosphere gives it a very different character from other Grand Slams. Tennis.title: US Open: Is Zheng Qinwen going to give us another Emma Raducanu moment in New York?
Tennis.summary: US Open: Is Zheng Qinwen going to give us another Emma Raducanu moment in New York? thenationalnews.com
Tennis.body:
Five years ago at the US Open, Emma Raducanu, then ranked 150th in the world, pulled off a miracle and became the first qualifier in tennis history to win a Grand Slam title. In June this year, Maja Chwalinska, ranked 114th, was one victory away from replicating that feat as she stormed to the French Open final as a qualifier. She ultimately lost the title match to Mirra Andreeva.

Zheng broke down in tears during her post-match press conference that day at Roland Garros. She had won just seven matches in the six events she had contested since returning to the tour in February. She was searching for a spark to ignite the competitive fire within her that had been missing throughout her comeback thus far.

Tennis.title: US Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka edges into semi-finals with three-set win over Linda Noskova
Tennis.summary: US Open 2026: Aryna Sabalenka edges into semi-finals with three-set win over Linda Noskova Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka maintained her hopes of a third successive US Open title with a battling three-set win over Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova in an absorbing quarter-final - a result that retains her status as world No 1 for at least one more day.

The 28-year-old beat Noskova 7-6 (7-1) 3-6 7-6 (10-7), coming through two tie-breaks - and a 4-2 deficit in the final set - as she sealed victory with a second-serve ace to set up a meeting with Jessica Pegula.

Tennis.title: Tiafoe consoles tearful Michelsen after remarkable comeback
Tennis.summary: Frances Tiafoe comes from two sets and a break down to beat Alex Michelsen in a thrilling comeback to reach the US Open semi-finals.
Tennis.body:
Frances Tiafoe came from two sets and a break down to beat fellow American Alex Michelsen in a thrilling comeback to reach the US Open semi-finals. Eleventh seed Tiafoe was outplayed by world number 46 Michelsen for the first half of the match, but battled back from 5-3 down in the third set to ignite a remarkable turnaround.

In a final set of multiple breaks and swings of momentum, Tiafoe triumphed in the 10-point tie-break to win 5-7 3-6 7-5 6-3 7-6 (10-6). Victory means 28-year-old Tiafoe reaches his third US Open semi-final in five years, where he will play defending champion Carlos Alcaraz or American eighth seed Ben Shelton.

Tennis.title: Hewett and Reid bid for sixth US Open title
Tennis.summary: Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid start their bid for a sixth wheelchair doubles title at the US Open with a dominant victory in New York.
Tennis.body:
Alfie Hewett and Gordon Reid started their bid for a sixth wheelchair doubles title at the US Open with a dominant opening victory in New York. Playing Frenchman Stephane Houdet and China's Zhenxu Ji, the British top seeds sealed a 6-3 6-1 win to progress to the semi-finals.

They will next face Japan's Tokito Oda and Argentina's Gustavo Fernandez, the 2025 champions at Flushing Meadows. Hewett, 28, and Reid, 34, have 25 Grand Slam doubles titles as a pair and begin their singles campaigns on Wednesday.

Tennis.title: Sabalenka thought title defence was over before US Open fightback
Tennis.summary: Aryna Sabalenka battles back to beat sixth seed Linda Noskova in three sets and advance to the semi-finals.
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka thought she had lost her US Open crown before battling back to beat Linda Noskova in three sets and advance to the semi-finals. Taken to a deciding set for the first time in this year's tournament, the two-time defending champion trailed 4-2 in the third set and later 2-0 in the tie-break before recovering to close out the win in a little under two and a half hours.

It was the 28-year-old's 19th consecutive win at the tournament, having not tasted defeat since the 2023 final, while she becomes the first woman since Serena Williams in 2016 to reach six successive semi-finals at Flushing Meadows.

Tennis.title: From match point to US Open exit
Tennis.summary: France's Arthur Gea held match point to become the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final - three hours later he was out of the US Open.
Tennis.body:
France's Arthur Gea was one point away from being the first lucky loser to reach a Grand Slam quarter-final - but three hours later he was out of the US Open. Gea, 21, was unable to convert a match point in a third-set tie-break against Dutch opponent Botic van de Zandschulp, then could not serve out victory in the fourth set of a gruelling fourth-round contest.

Van de Zandschulp took full advantage to escape from the jaws of defeat, going on to secure a 3-6 6-7 (0-7) 7-6 (9-7) 7-6 (7-3) 6-4 win after five hours and 13 minutes - the fourth longest match on record at Flushing Meadows.

Tennis.title: Gauff's statement win completes stacked US Open last eight
Tennis.summary: Coco Gauff powers past teenage star Iva Jovic as the top six seeds reach the US Open women's quarter-finals for the first time in 28 years.
Tennis.body:
It was not so long ago that Coco Gauff was the teenage sensation looking to cause an upset at the US Open. Now, at the grand old age of 22, she is the Grand Slam champion and leading WTA Tour star who drew on her experience to deal with talented 18-year-old Iva Jovic at Flushing Meadows.

Fourth seed Gauff found her finest level of the fortnight to beat fellow American Jovic in a 6-1 6-4 win and secure her place in the quarter-finals. Gauff's comfortable progress ensured the top six seeds have reached the US Open women's last eight for the first time since 1998, further illustrating the strength in depth at the top of the WTA Tour.

Tennis.title: 'We're not robots'
Tennis.summary: The chaotic nature of the men's draw has been a sharp contrast to the relative calm of the women's - but anyone can still win the US Open titles.
Tennis.body:
Talent, athleticism and commitment are not nearly enough to become a Grand Slam singles champion. Possessing the confidence that you can beat anyone on the biggest stage - where the eyes of the world are fixed on you and there is no place to hide - is arguably the most important characteristic a player can have.

Unwavering belief. Or, as former US Open runner-up Taylor Fritz describes it, delusion. Fritz is one of the current crop of leading men yet to get his hands on one of the sport's major prizes. The world number 10 is also one of the guys who has blown what looked like a golden opportunity to win this year's US Open.

The British number one has endured a tough year with injury and illness restricting her court time, and she was knocked out in the first round at the French Open. But on the slick grasscourts, the 2021 US Open champion, who has recently reunited with her former coach Andrew Richardson, produced a confident display against the qualifier as she began her preparations for Wimbledon.

"The way I was moving, the way I was expressing, just the whole package, not necessarily the tennis, just how I was acting on the court," the 23-year-old said. "I really enjoyed it and I think that's something that I want to take forward in all my matches and really embrace this grass-court season."

Tennis.title: Sabalenka overcomes tricky Townsend test at US Open
Tennis.summary: Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka emulates Serena Williams by overcoming Taylor Townsend to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final.
Tennis.body:
Two-time defending champion Aryna Sabalenka emulated Serena Williams as she eventually overpowered American Taylor Townsend to reach a sixth straight US Open quarter-final. A topsy-turvy contest featured 10 breaks of serve, but Sabalenka recovered from 3-1 down in the second serve to seal a 6-4 6-3 victory with a fifth consecutive game.

It was the Belarusian's 18th consecutive win at the tournament, extending her three-year unbeaten streak following back-to-back triumphs in 2024 and 2025. Sabalenka, 28, is the first woman to reach six consecutive singles quarter-finals at Flushing Meadows since American great Williams in 2016.

The Olympic champion, who had to come through qualifying to reach the main draw, found herself 5-0 and match point down in the third set against Keys.

But Zheng held firm and reeled off seven games in a row to secure a remarkable 1-6 7-6 (7-3) 7-5 victory over the 22nd seed and crowd favourite. Keys, who won the 2025 Australian Open, appeared to be cruising towards a commanding victory after wrapping up the opening set in just 23 minutes.

Tennis.title: Emma Raducanu’s US Open triumph five years on, told by her opponents
Tennis.summary: Emma Raducanu’s US Open triumph five years on, told by her opponents The i Paper
Tennis.body:
FLUSHING MEADOWS — “Is it really five years?” says one player incredulously when I ask them what they were doing the night Emma Raducanu won the US Open. For many of us, it feels like yesterday. Raducanu’s run from qualifying to the title, never achieved at a grand slam before or since, has shaped the last five years in British tennis like few three-week periods ever have. She became and remains this country’s biggest star in women’s tennis, her every match, interview, coaching change and practice session closely followed and scrutinised.

It is typical of the rocky road Raducanu, now 23, has ridden since becoming US Open champion that she is not even here in New York to look back at the half-decade that has passed. The Big Apple has not been a happy hunting ground in that time either: she has won just two matches at this tournament since she won it.

Tennis.summary: US Open: Aryna Sabalenka complains of cannabis smell during win over Kamilla Rakhimova to reach fourth round Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Aryna Sabalenka complained to the umpire about a strong smell of cannabis that was present duing her third-round win over Kamilla Rakhimova at the US Open. The world No 1 came through in straight sets, beating her unseeded opponent 6-3 6-4 on Louis Armstrong Stadium, but after racing into a 3-0 lead in the opening set, Sabalenka complained to umpire Eva Asderaki-Moore at the first changeover.

"I was like, 'Guys, you can do whatever, you can smoke whatever, you can relax as much as you can, but please to not do it around the tennis courts'," Sabalenka told reporters afterwards. "It's a bit tricky to handle that smell while you're trying to compete at your best."

Harriet Dart and Francesca Jones fell to seeded players as British interest in the US Open singles ended in the second round. Dart said she felt "under the weather" during her 6-2 6-2 defeat by Czech 25th seed Marie Bouzkova as temperatures reached 30C in New York.

Her loss meant Jones was the last Briton standing in either singles draw, and she acquitted herself well before falling 6-4 6-4 to 14th seed and rising American star Iva Jovic.

Tennis.title: Kyrgios given one-month ban for positive cocaine test
Tennis.summary: Nick Kyrgios is eligible to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine.
Tennis.body:
Nick Kyrgios is eligible to return to tennis after accepting a one-month ban for testing positive for cocaine. The Australian, 31, was provisionally suspended on 4 August after a sample he submitted during the Mallorca Open in June was found to contain benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

Kyrgios told investigators from the International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA) that he used cocaine at a nightclub in Magaluf in the early hours of 20 June. He played his first-round match at the Mallorca tournament two days later, losing in straight sets to compatriot Adam Walton.

Tennis.title: US Open: Naomi Osaka urges social media influencers in attendance to respect tennis 'etiquette' after second-round win
Tennis.summary: US Open: Naomi Osaka urges social media influencers in attendance to respect tennis 'etiquette' after second-round win Sky Sports
Tennis.body:
Naomi Osaka urged the growing number of social media influencers at the US Open to respect the sport's "etiquette" following her second-round win over Katerina Siniakova. The issue has become a talking point at the tournament following Osaka's opening win over Anastasia Zakharova on Monday, in which viral videos have since surfaced of some influencers not paying attention to the tennis.

After overcoming a mid-match wobble to beat Katerina Siniakova 6-2 5-7 6-1 and reach the third round in New York, Osaka said on the issue: "I think obviously if you come to a sporting event, you have to respect the sport.

Tennis.title: US Open: Carlos Alcaraz planning more breaks in 'impossible' tennis schedule after more than four months out with a wrist injury
Tennis.summary: US Open: Carlos Alcaraz planning more breaks in 'impossible' tennis schedule after more than four months out with a wrist injury Sky Sports

The Spaniard, who returned to action after a lengthy layoff due to a wrist injury sustained in April to defend his US Open title, said the demands of the schedule made it impossible for players to compete in every major event without risking burnout.

Golf.title: How history points to another Solheim Cup thriller
Golf.summary: With no more than one point separating the teams at the past three Solheim Cups played in Europe there is every reason to expect that this week's contest will be just as exciting, writes Iain Carter.
Golf.body:
Recent history suggests this week's Solheim Cup will be another epic clash to follow hot on the heels of Great Britain and Ireland's dramatic victory over the United States in the Walker Cup.

The extraordinary climax at Lahinch last Sunday, where GB&I won with the last putt of the match, evoked memories of the past three Solheim Cups staged in Europe. Three years ago in Spain the contest ended in a dramatic 14-14 tie to allow a delirious European team to hold on to the trophy, having initially wrestled it from American hands with a single-point victory at Gleneagles in 2019.

Golf.title: “The power battle for golf, and its biggest players, might not be over just yet” | Media Centre
Golf.summary: “The power battle for golf, and its biggest players, might not be over just yet” | Media Centre Loughborough University
Golf.body:
“Five years on from LIV’s inception, golf’s power battle appears to have swung back in favour of the PGA. However, it may feel like victory but at a cost. The PGA have had to function without some of the biggest names in the sport for the last few years and has had to bolster their prize money as a result, even going so far as to create a for-profit business model that offers the players future equity stakes in the company.

“Viewed through this lens, the entry of LIV Golf, while controversial, did act as a catalyst for both innovation and defensive consolidation within the sport. The response from the PGA Tour was immediate and material, most notably through significant increases in prize money and the acceleration of strategic alignment with the DP World Tour. The introduction of PGA Tour cards for the top performers in the Race to Dubai was a clear signal of intent: to strengthen institutional ties and reinforce the traditional ecosystem in the face of external disruption.

Golf.title: This U.S. star has been sick. At Solheim Cup, she’ll need to find strength
Golf.summary: U.S. star Angel Yin is playing in the Solheim Cup in the Netherlands after a two-month break from competition for a stomach illness. The post This U.S. star has been sick. At Solheim Cup, she’ll need to find strength appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The first signs that Angel Yin was not well came at the KPMG Women’s PGA Championship in Minnesota in late June. Yin, who was then ranked 16th in the world, opened with a solid one-under 71 — then checked herself into a hospital, complaining of stomach pain. The next day, Yin was on the back on the course, at shin-kicking Hazeltine National, where she dug deep and posted another 71 to make the cut by two. But by Saturday morning, Yin, who is 27, was back in the hospital with no hope of playing the third round. She was hospitalized for another six days before flying home to Florida. She would have weeks more of gastrointestinal challenges ahead of her.

Over the next two months, Yin was unable to return to competition and limited her diet to the likes of rice, boiled chicken and cooked vegetables, she told Golfweek’s Beth Ann Nichols. Yin wasn’t trying to lose weight but she did: 35 pounds in all. In late August, she returned to the LPGA, at the FM Championship at TPC Boston. It did not go well, at least not in terms of the numbers on her scorecards: 81-76. More worrying still, the Solheim Cup, for which Yin had qualified months earlier, was less than two weeks away.

Golf.title: 9 revealing findings inside LIV’s bankruptcy filings
Golf.summary: LIV Golf filed hundreds of pages of documents in bankruptcy court this week. These 9 learnings stuck out to us. The post 9 revealing findings inside LIV’s bankruptcy filings appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy, which means much of its business operations — both in the past and in the future — have been forced into the public eye ahead of its various court hearings. In total, LIV’s representation filed hundreds of pages of documents Tuesday evening and Wednesday in advance of a Wednesday afternoon hearing in front of Judge Michael B. Kaplan in New Jersey.

We pored through those documents and picked out several findings that help tell the story of where LIV has been and where it hopes to go. Check them out below. For LIV Golf to come back in a different form, it has secured an agreement with BC Partners’ credit division to fund its court-monitored bankruptcy interim as well as exit financing to support the league moving forward … so long as players commit by early October.

Golf.title: The most popular wedge on the PGA Tour also was most successful
Golf.summary: Titleist's Vokey wedges again led the count of PGA Tour winning wedges in 2026, with two different models leading the way. The post The most popular wedge on the PGA Tour also was most successful appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Once again, the winningest wedge on the PGA Tour was also the most played wedge on the PGA Tour. With 21 victories in 2026, Vokey again led the winning-wedge count — while also making up 52 percent of all gap, sand and lob wedges on the PGA Tour this past season.

Other brands had excellent years, too. TaylorMade recorded seven wins with its new MG5 platform, including three from a non-contracted player. Cleveland also had multiple non-contracted wins, in addition to recording a major (Ryan Fox, Open Championship) with its RTZ wedges.

Golf.body:
Play this year doesn’t. But previously it had under the U.S. Ryder Cup team’s qualification system, and the elimination of it, announced Wednesday, represents a significant change for the Americans, who, next year, will be looking to win the Cup on European turf for the first time since 1993.

“I have worked diligently with our team and am pleased to implement a new qualifying process for the 2027 U.S. Ryder Cup Team,” U.S. captain Jim Furyk said in a release from the PGA of America.

Golf.body:
Padraig Harrington has long held a reputation as one of the game’s hardest workers, and in more recent years, the 55-year-old has also acquired a devoted following on social media, where he regularly dispenses swing advice and course-management wisdom.

But a recent online escapade threw the three-time major winner (and three-time U.S. Senior Open winner) for a serious loop. Harrington became the latest player to take on the DP World Tour’s “Chase the Ace” challenge. The goal? Make a hole-in-one on a par-3 with 500 chances.

Golf.title: How to put spin on your pitch shots (the right way!), according to a top teacher
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Joey Wuertemberger explains that proper technique to put spin on your pitch shots around the green. The post How to put spin on your pitch shots (the right way!), according to a top teacher appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
One of the biggest misconceptions in wedge play is that you have to do something special with your hands to make the ball check. Players try to cut across it, flip the clubhead under the ball or add excessive loft. What those types of players fail to understand is that spin isn’t a trick or gimmick. It’s simply the result of creating the right conditions between the clubface and the ball at impact.

Clean contact, clean grooves, enough speed and the proper amount of loft create friction. And friction is what allows the ball to grab the face, launch with control and spin when it hits the green.

Golf.title: Ryder Cup race a 'big part' of Lowry's motivation
Golf.summary: Shane Lowry says it is time to get himself "in gear" if he is to secure his spot on Europe's Ryder Cup team for Adare Manor next year.
Golf.body:
Shane Lowry says it is time to get himself "in gear" if he is to secure his spot on Europe's Ryder Cup team for Adare Manor next year. The 2019 Open champion is in the field at the Irish Open this week, with the qualification process for the 2027 Ryder Cup, to be held in County Limerick from 17-19 September, having commenced last month.

Irishman Lowry was a member of the European teams in 2021, 2023 and 2025, holing the winning putt in the latter event at Bethpage Black. The 39-year-old has, however, fallen from 26th to 53rd in the world rankings over the course of 2026 in a season characterised by frustrating near-misses.

Golf.title: The lessons of LIV Golf’s failure
Golf.summary: The lessons of LIV Golf’s failure Financial Times
Golf.body:
Roula Khalaf, Editor of the FT, selects her favourite stories in this weekly newsletter. Four years ago, LIV Golf promised “golf, but louder”. Protracted 72-hole tournaments would be swapped for higher-octane 54-hole team events with shotgun starts — simultaneous tee-offs at different holes — blaring music and huge payouts for players. Backed by $5bn-plus of investment from Saudi Arabia, it was an attempt to disrupt the sedate world of golf and build soft power for Riyadh. After the Saudi Public Investment Fund said in April it would pull funding, LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy protection this week. It hopes to launch a “LIV 2.0” backed by buyout firm BC Partners. But LIV 1.0 is over, along with Saudi hopes of building a rival power centre in golf — though not Riyadh’s newfound clout in many other sports.

LIV Golf was the flagship of a broader Saudi sports investment strategy. This was often justifiably portrayed as an exercise in “sportswashing” the kingdom’s record of human rights abuses. But there was something more to the investment. It was another way to diversify the economy away from oil, and hosting sports events could help make the kingdom more attractive to tourists. And it was intended to get young Saudis off their couches — but involved in pursuits not connected to politics.

Golf.title: Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm deserve no sympathy, any PGA Tour deal must cost $100m minimum
Golf.summary: Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm deserve no sympathy, any PGA Tour deal must cost $100m minimum talkSPORT
Golf.body:
There are only two golfers that truly matter in the LIV Golf debacle: Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm. On the one hand, they hold all the cards. On the other, they are in complete limbo - with millions of dollars and the integrity of their careers shrouded in uncertainty.

The golf league formerly known as Saudi-backed is not giving up - this is more an acceptance of the total $5billion nightmare that was LIV Golf 1.0 and a desperate attempt to start fresh.

Golf.title: Pinehurst Resort's newest course, Pinehurst No. 11, to open this spring
Golf.summary: The opening of Pinehurst No. 11, on land made unruly by decades of mining, will add another marquee course to the famed North Carolina resort. The post Pinehurst Resort’s newest course, Pinehurst No. 11, to open this spring appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Pinehurst Resort has announced an opening date for the latest addition to its world-renowned course lineup: Pinehurst No. 11 will welcome play on March 29, 2027. Tee times will be available exclusively to resort guests, and bookings open today.

Like most big happenings at Pinehurst, this one is a big deal in destination golf, with some suitably big names attached. Bill Coore and Ben Crenshaw designed No. 11, with their associate Ryan Farrow handling the shaping. Coore and Crenshaw are no strangers to this swath of the Sandhills; they have been visiting since the 1970s and orchestrated the celebrated restoration of Pinehurst No. 2 more than a decade ago.

Golf.title: McIlroy warns tours have ‘decisions to make’ as LIV Golf exodus edges closer
Golf.summary: McIlroy warns tours have ‘decisions to make’ as LIV Golf exodus edges closer The Guardian
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy believes traditional tours will soon have “decisions to make” as a player exodus from LIV Golf edges closer. LIV filing for bankruptcy in the United States on Tuesday means its deals with several high-profile golfers will soon be invalid, leaving them free to negotiate a route back to the PGA and DP World Tours. When asked whether remaining with LIV in its planned, far-less lucrative form would hold appeal, McIlroy was characteristically candid. “I’m not in their shoes but LIV at the start looked a lot more attractive than what LIV 2.0 might be from a financial standpoint,” said the Masters champion.

The Chapter 11 bankruptcy filing – stating around $45m (£33.2m) is owed to players – represented LIV’s latest step in rebooting the business due to the removal of funding from Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund (PIF). Sources familiar with the situation insist contracts have not yet been breached. Terms in place with star names are now unaffordable for LIV. Contracts will inevitably either be renegotiated or cancelled.

Golf.title: What next for LIV Golf's star players, and its fight for survival?
Golf.summary: Golf's main tours are expecting a lot of interest in rejoining from LIV golfers – but the path back might not be so easy.
Golf.body:
The DP World Tour has said it has had a "high volume" of interest from LIV Golf players and is exploring ways to accommodate those who leave the breakaway league. It comes as LIV Golf filed for bankruptcy protection in the US on Tuesday, as it attempts to restructure for a "new era" next year.

LIV owes at least $45m (£33m) to 14 current and former players. Its golfers, including star names like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm, can now opt to leave, rather than being obliged to see out their contracts in LIV 2.0 which is aiming to launch next year.

Golf.title: 'It's going to be different': Rory McIlroy reacts to President Trump's likely Irish Open visit
Golf.summary: President Donald Trump is expected to attend the 2026 Irish Open, and on Wednesday Rory McIlroy shared his opinion on Trump's visit. The post ‘It’s going to be different’: Rory McIlroy reacts to President Trump’s likely Irish Open visit appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy is the needle at the Irish Open. As the undisputed greatest golfer to hail from the island of Ireland, arguably the greatest active golfer alive and the defending champion, McIlroy will have the fans fully behind him this week.

But, at least for one day of the event, McIlroy is expected to have some competition in the fame and attention departments — when President Trump makes an appearance. This week’s Amgen Irish Open is being held at Trump International Golf Links in Doonbeg, Ireland, and President Trump is expected to attend at least one of the weekend rounds.

Golf.title: Troubled league LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection in US
Golf.summary: Troubled league LIV Golf files for bankruptcy protection in US Al Jazeera
Golf.body:
Less than five years after it held its first event and created a schism in professional golf, LIV Golf has filed for bankruptcy protection in New Jersey, United States. The Chapter 11 bankruptcy, or reorganisation bankruptcy, filed on Tuesday, allows the debtor to remain in possession and operate its business, according to US Courts.

The move offers a rare window into the league’s financial state, with LIV Golf owing between $500m and $1bn in estimated liabilities to at least 1,000 creditors, including star players like Bryson DeChambeau and Jon Rahm.

Golf.title: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: what's next for the sport?
Golf.summary: LIV Golf in financial turmoil: what's next for the sport? Yahoo News UK
Golf.body:
The breakaway golf tour, launched with much fanfare, billions of dollars of investment and a string of the world's best players, in 2021. But on Tuesday it filed for bankruptcy protection in the US.

Bankruptcy protection is a way of keeping a company alive while it restructures its debts. In this case, LIV would be moving from being financed by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF), which pulled out in April, to being supported by BC Partners, a British investment firm.

Golf.title: LIV Golf namedrops Premier League club in $500million bankruptcy decision
Golf.summary: LIV Golf namedrops Premier League club in $500million bankruptcy decision talksport.com
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has used Leeds United as an example of how they intend to survive as the breakaway league filed for bankruptcy on Tuesday. The struggling golf circuit is restructuring for what it describes as 'LIV Golf 2.0' - with liabilities of between $500million and $1billion (£370m-£739m) from the pre-existing version.

The Saudi-backed breakaway tour invested $5bn (£3.6bn) in luring golf’s top talents away from the PGA Tour and created a serious fracture in the sport. However, the tour's long-term future was plunged into doubt earlier this year when the Public Investment Fund [PIF] opted to discontinue its funding beyond the 2026 season.

Golf.title: LIV Golf files for bankruptcy: What we know
Golf.summary: LIV Golf filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy Tuesday, confirming what was long-rumored: it owes a lot of money and plans to restructure. The post LIV Golf files for bankruptcy: What we know appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Following months of rumors, lawsuits and financial unease, LIV Golf has officially filed for bankruptcy. The rival golf league that took on the status quo in pro golf has filed for Chapter 11 bankruptcy in New Jersey, formally marking some end to, as Jon Rahm called it Tuesday morning, LIV Golf 1.0. Chapter 11 is best understood as a corporate restructuring mechanism with intent to continue.

The filing arrived shortly after 4 p.m. ET and includes some information not previously released, like money owed to players and various vendors that have recently taken LIV to court for unpaid services. Also Tuesday, we had confirmation of LIV’s “lead investor” that CEO Scott O’Neil first mentioned a month ago; O’Neil also wrote a letter to fans about LIV’s next phase.

Golf.title: 'False' Charley Hull story shut down by her Solheim Cup captains
Golf.summary: Charley Hull's Solheim Cup captains cleared up the reason for her late arrival to a Tuesday-morning practice round in the Netherlands. The post ‘False’ Charley Hull story shut down by her Solheim Cup captains appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Why was Charley Hull, Team Europe’s biggest star, late for her Tuesday-morning practice round at Bernardus Golf in the Netherlands? The query was directed at Europe’s captain, Anna Nordqvist, and her three lieutenants, Caroline Hedwall, Mel Reid and Anne van Dam, at their captain’s press conference.

Reid did, because, as she saw it, she had some rumors to quash. “This could be a full story,” Reid began. “Charley Hull was the first one to bed last night at 8 o’clock and first one on the bus this morning. She doesn’t even drink, so that’s a completely false story it’s been misquoted. She was late to the tee because I was responsible for her, so I’ll take a little bit of responsibility to that. But she just thought her tee time was a little bit later, and trying to drag Charley Hull off a driving range is a feat in any tournament, especially a Solheim. So yeah it’s a completely false story.”

Golf.title: LIV files for bankruptcy protection with over $45m owed to players
Golf.summary: LIV Golf has filed for bankruptcy protection with at least $45m (£33m) owed to players, who will now have the option to leave.
Golf.body:
LIV Golf has filed for bankruptcy protection with at least $45m (£33m) owed to players, who will now have the option to leave. A Chapter 11 petition, which LIV says is to "preserve the company's business" as it attempts to restructure after Saudi Arabia withdrew its multibillion-dollar funding, was filed in the United States on Tuesday.

The breakaway league says it has found a new investor in BC Partners, following the decision in April by Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund (PIF) to pull its funding. Documents in the petition outline money owed to LIV Golf's creditors with the 30 largest unsecured claims. Two-time major winner Jon Rahm tops that list with an unsecured claim of $7.5m (£5.5m).

Golf.title: The next phase of LIV Golf
Golf.summary: The next phase of LIV Golf livgolf.com
Golf.body:
Thank you for embracing our players, our teams, and a new way of experiencing professional golf. LIV Golf was created to bring the world’s best players to fans around the world, and thanks to your support, in a few short years we built a truly global league.

We put team golf on the world stage consistently and combined elite competition with music, culture, art, and energy in a way global golf fans rarely get to see. Fans 20 years younger than golf's traditional viewership showed up onsite and through our content. We brought world-class players and teams to new markets. We welcomed major global broadcast and marketing partners. And, most importantly, we built a passionate community of fans who believe in what LIV Golf can become.

Golf.body:
We know where Jon Rahm is playing this week. But where the two-time major champion and LIV Golf pro will tee it up next year is an open question. Rahm is in Ireland this week to compete in the 2026 Amgen Irish Open, a DP World Tour event that’s drawing an impressive field from LIV and PGA Tour ranks, including Rory McIlroy.

Golf.title: Rules Guy: I made an ace — with my playing partner's club! Is it legal?
Golf.summary: If you make a hole-in-one with another player's club, does it count? Rules Guy has the answer — and it might surprise you. The post Rules Guy: I made an ace — with my playing partner’s club! Is it legal? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The Rules of Golf are tricky! Thankfully, we’’e got the guru. Our Rules Guy knows the book front to back. Got a question? He’s got all the answers. A friendly four-ball match. We reach a par-3, and my buddy looks to pull his 6-iron only to realize he left it on a prior hole. Another player offered up his 6 and, sure enough, my pal jars his first-ever ace. We counted it…but I’m thinking he’d normally incur a penalty, even though he only had 13 clubs in his bag at the time. For what it’s worth, he did later get back the missing club. – John Jay, Conneaut Lake, PA

An interesting question, worthy of the original John Jay, who as you no doubt know was a Founding Father, the first Chief Justice of the United States, and the second governor of New York. But we digress.

Golf.title: Irish Open will feel 'different' with Trump visit
Golf.summary: Rory McIlroy admits this year's Irish Open will feel like a "different" spectacle given US President Donald Trump's anticipated visit during the tournament.
Golf.body:
Rory McIlroy admits this year's Irish Open will feel like a "different" spectacle given US President Donald Trump's anticipated visit during the tournament's latter stages. Trump is expected to attend the event - which is being held at his resort in the County Clare village of Doonbeg - this weekend as part of a two-day visit to Ireland.

McIlroy has previously played golf with Trump, who earlier this year praised the Northern Irishman's accomplishments on the course after winning back-to-back Masters titles. "It's going to be different, but the one thing I'd say is his golf resorts have hosted PGA Tour events, European Tour events, LIV events," McIlroy told BBC Sport NI's Stephen Watson.

Golf.title: ‘I still have a contract with LIV that I’m more than willing to fulfil’ — Jon Rahm on facing career uncertainty
Golf.summary: ‘I still have a contract with LIV that I’m more than willing to fulfil’ — Jon Rahm on facing career uncertainty Irish Independent
Golf.body:
If LIV’s Jon Rahm dances his way between the dunes and bunkers at Doonbeg as deftly as he dodges questions about his future, he has a third Irish Open title in the bag. Bobbing and weaving like Urtain — the Basque José Manuel Ibar Azpiazu who became EBU heavyweight champion in 1970 and 1971 — the two-time Irish Open winner would not be pinned on the ropes about his future with the breakaway circuit.

Amid reports from the Financial Times that LIV Golf is looking to file for bankruptcy protection in the wake of Saudi Arabia’s PIF pulling its funding, leaving CEO Scott O’Neil scrambling to find backers to LIV Golf 2.0, the Spanish star was giving little away as wind and rain, mixed with occasional sunny spells, kept the players on their toes in west Clare.

Golf.title: As Cabot Revelstoke nears completion, excitement comes with the territory
Golf.summary: Sometimes the pursuit of exquisite golf means crossing oceans, although for Cabot Revelstoke it’s just a border away. The post As Cabot Revelstoke nears completion, excitement comes with the territory appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Rod Whitman has spent more than four decades building great golf courses and almost no time building the Rod Whitman brand. At 72, the Canadian-born course designer has quietly assembled one of the game’s most respected résumés. After apprenticing under Pete Dye and shaping for Bill Coore and Ben Crenshaw, Whitman struck out on his own in 1984, going on to solo-design Cabot Links and shape acclaimed courses like Friars Head and Old Sandwich. His work has drawn a spotlight that Whitman hasn’t clamored for himself. He doesn’t have a computer or a publicist. He isn’t on social media.

“I feel like the past 40 years, I’ve mostly just been working,” he says on a recent morning from the tee of a short, downhill par 3. It was just past dawn, the sun peaking over the mountains of British Columbia, and Whitman was busy with his latest job, putting the finishing touches on Cabot Revelstoke, his own design and the centerpiece of Cabot’s plans for a new alpine destination.
Golf.copy:
Rod Whitman has spent more than four decades building great golf courses and almost no time building the Rod Whitman brand. At 72, the Canadian-born course designer has quietly assembled one of the game’s most respected résumés. After apprenticing under Pete Dye and shaping for Bill Coore and Ben Crenshaw, Whitman struck out on his own in 1984, going on to solo-design Cabot Links and shape acclaimed courses like Friars Head and Old Sandwich. His work has drawn a spotlight that Whitman hasn’t clamored for himself. He doesn’t have a computer or a publicist. He isn’t on social media.

“I feel like the past 40 years, I’ve mostly just been working,” he says on a recent morning from the tee of a short, downhill par 3. It was just past dawn, the sun peaking over the mountains of British Columbia, and Whitman was busy with his latest job, putting the finishing touches on Cabot Revelstoke, his own design and the centerpiece of Cabot’s plans for a new alpine destination.

Golf.title: For the second-generation ZXi irons, Srixon turned to a legendary partner
Golf.summary: Srixon's second-generation ZXi irons improve on the popular line with a new partnership with one of the game's legendary forging houses. The post For the second-generation ZXi irons, Srixon turned to a legendary partner appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When it comes to forged irons, the name Endo Manufacturing can stop gearheads in their tracks. Srixon is counting on it with their second-generation ZXi irons. In releasing the updated line, which again includes the ZXi7, ZXi5 and ZXiU irons, along with the new ZXi5+ players distance iron, Srixon is announcing that all four irons are forged by the legendary Japanese forging house.

“We’ve been working with Endo for a long time,” Srixon Senior Product Manager Casey Schultz told GOLF. “We’ve had a relationship with them in the past, but this is the first time that we’ve been able to really kind of announce the fact that every single iron is being made there.”

Golf.title: The September golf schedule? It's for the diehards
Golf.summary: The Tour Championship is over and football season is right around the corner, but some of the best golf of the year is right in front of us. The post The September golf schedule? It’s for the diehards appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
There’s a common misconception that the golf season ends in August. Next up: the California Swing, five months out. Or, for the real casuals, the Masters, eight months away. But that’s far from reality. Your uncle Mark probably knows about the Memorial and U.S. Open and Pebble Beach and that crazy 16th hole at TPC Scottsdale, but it’s the true diehard, sicko golf fans who get excited for all the wonderful September golf ahead and things like Lahinch (last week’s Walker Cup venue), an Irish Open (names like Rahm, McIlroy and Koepka are playing) and Wentworth (host of the BMW Championship, the DP World Tour’s flagship event).

September is an intoxicating mix of team events and tournaments contested on old layouts that us lucky Americans get to watch in the mornings. That’s the best kind of golf, the golf you can watch when you wake up, when fall is approaching and it’s starting to get chilly in the States but not quite as cold as what it looks like on TV at Doughmore Beach, a few steps from where they’re playing the Irish Open at Trump International Golf Links & Hotel. (The coffee, with the smallest splash of cream, always tastes better too.)

Golf.title: This no-fuss training aid solves a common swing issue
Golf.summary: Since its inception in 2014, the Smart Ball remains wildly popular, and the Smart Ball Sleeve lets you attach it anywhere. The post This no-fuss training aid solves a common swing issue appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
When GOLF’s own Top 100 Teacher Martin Chuck created the Smart Ball, his goal was simple: Make a no-fuss training aid that actually solves a common swing issue. Just put the lanyard around your neck and the Smart Ball helps you keep your arms connected and your body rotating properly.

Since its inception in 2014, the Smart Ball remains wildly popular, and you’re still likely to find it in use on the practice tee at nearly every PGA Tour stop. Chuck has stepped things up with the Smart Ball Sleeve ($57 with a Smart Ball; tourstriker.com) — a clever, wearable accessory that lets you attach the Smart Ball almost anywhere: arms, legs, hips, you name it. And, of course, Chuck’s got video drills to go with it, educating you on exactly how this versatile tool can help you dial in your swing.

Golf.title: Flair, grip and durability? Why Asher checks those boxes
Golf.summary: In 2009, Asher set out to turn golf gloves into a fashion piece, and today the brand offers some of the most stylish gloves on the market. The post Flair, grip and durability? Why Asher checks those boxes appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Too often, we overlook or undervalue just how important our golf glove really is, only to realize how dreadful things can get when it goes bad. For many, a fine Cabretta leather glove — slightly thinner and more moisture-resistant than cowhide — is an essential component not only to playing well and maintaining your hold on the club but also to protecting your hand from calluses and blisters.

In 2009, Asher set out to turn this largely utilitarian accessory into a fashion piece, and today the brand offers some of the most stylish gloves on the market. They’re available in a wide range of colors and sizes for men and women to punch up any on-course outfit. Asher helps you add a little flair to your look while still providing the grip and durability you need.

Golf.title: Can Cleveland's new RTZ2 wedges handle real-world turf? We put them to the test
Golf.summary: Johnny Wunder and Jake Morrow traveled to Pinehurst to put the Cleveland RTZ2 wedges to the "game-time" test. Here are the results. The post Can Cleveland’s new RTZ2 wedges handle real-world turf? We put them to the test appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Wedge testing is a finicky thing. A lot of great work can be done in a fitting bay, without question. But you can’t put a metric for how important getting a bunch of wedges out on a course to just mess around is. You’ve seen us test a bunch of clubs in the technical way, but what about the “feel” way?

Well… Jake and I grabbed an armful of the new Cleveland RTZ2 wedges, kicked off our shoes and walked nine holes at The Cradle at Pinehurst. Sand-dusted turf, short targets, Sunday bags — an honest place to see what a leading edge actually does under pressure. Here’s what we learned.

Golf.title: GB&I make history with first Walker Cup since 2015
Golf.summary: Great Britain and Ireland produce the biggest comeback in Walker Cup history to defeat the United States and lift the trophy for the first time since 2015.
Golf.body:
Great Britain and Ireland produced the biggest comeback in Walker Cup history to defeat the United States and lift the trophy for the first time since 2015. At Lahinch in Ireland, the USA looked to be on the brink when they swept the morning foursomes to move just three-and-a-half points away from a sixth consecutive victory.

But GB&I picked up seven of the 10 points in the singles to clinch victory by 13-and-a-half points to 12-and-a-half and win for the first time in 11 years. Josh Hill had the winning moment as he defeated world number two Tyler Watts on the final hole of the last match on the course, and that sparked wild celebrations to mark a victory that seemed so unlikely after Sunday morning.

Golf.title: Is the Walker Cup golf's greatest team event? It's been making the case
Golf.summary: The Walker Cup is in a great spot to become golf's greatest team event, because it’s all about the golfers, the golf and the host courses. The post Is the Walker Cup golf’s greatest team event? It’s been making the case appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Did you watch this Walker Cup at Lahinch, in Ireland? Maybe you were one of the 8,000 or so people on hand, watching up close. (Single-day tickets were about $50; kids were free.) Maybe you were watching on Golf Channel, with the American Curtis Cup star Emilia Migliaccio Doran and the former GB&I Walker Cup player Paul McGinley presiding. Poor McGinley, about the most refreshing voice in golf broadcasting today and an Irishman’s Irishman. He must be worn out. He was wearing his big heart on his green sleeve as he practically begged the home 10 to scratch out this half-point or that one.

In the end, his prayers were answered. In this 51st edition of the Walker Cup, the two-day event that unfolds with stunning speed, Great Britain and Ireland defeated a stacked American team, 13.5 to 12.5. Sunday afternoon, in the decisive singles play, GB&I won seven matches, halved two and lost one. GB&I won the event for the first time since 2015. It was amazing.

Golf.title: Team GB&I storms back to shock the U.S. and win the Walker Cup
Golf.summary: Team Great Britain & Ireland won seven of 10 points during Sunday Singles to complete an improbable Walker Cup comeback. The post Team GB&I storms back to shock the U.S. and win the Walker Cup appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Team Great Britain and Ireland are Walker Cup champions once again — and they did so in improbable fashion. Entering the final singles session on Sunday afternoon at Lahinch Golf Club, Team USA looked to be on their way to a sixth consecutive victory in the biennial team competition as they held a 9.5 to 6.5 advantage. However, thanks to a historic final session that saw GB&I win seven of the available 10 points, the team from across the pond completed the comeback for a 13.5 to 12.5 victory.

“I believed in the team the whole time,” said GB&I captain Dean Robertson. “I’m so proud of them. Just so special.” After Team USA swept the morning foursomes session, the three-point lead entering the final session looked all but insurmountable. Needing seven points in the final singles session, GB&I’s margin for error was razor thin. Luckily, many of them saved their best golf for last.
