Golf.title: 5 keys for fixing the 'chicken wing' in your golf swing
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Kellie Stenzel explains five keys for fixing the dreaded "chicken wing" in your golf swing. The post 5 keys for fixing the ‘chicken wing’ in your golf swing appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
If you struggle with a “chicken wing” in your golf swing, I’ve got good news: it can be fixed. Part of the reason it is so important to take lessons from a great instructor is that the chicken wing is often a necessary compensation for an earlier issue in the swing. In other words, simply trying to eliminate the chicken wing may not fix the problem. You first need to understand why it is happening.

Here are five things you can do to fix your chicken-wing swing. If you are looking for a quick fix, a split-hand drill can certainly help with the chicken wing. Because the hands are separated on the grip, the lead elbow will almost automatically fold and point down. This is the opposite of a chicken wing, where the elbows tend to separate as the club is pulled away from the ground. It’s a great drill to help you feel what the lead arm and elbow should be doing through impact and into the release.

Golf.title: Asian Tour CEO on the Pivot From LIV Golf to DP World Tour
Golf.summary: Asian Tour CEO on the Pivot From LIV Golf to DP World Tour golfraw.com
Golf.body:

Golf.title: 'A lot to play for': Paul Casey makes emotional vow after taking lead at European Masters
Golf.summary: Paul Casey will be playing for more than himself on Sunday. After taking the 54-hole lead at the European Masters, he made an emotional vow. The post ‘A lot to play for’: Paul Casey makes emotional vow after taking lead at European Masters appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
It has been a while since Paul Casey was in this spot, holding a 54-hole lead with a chance to add to his trophy case. But after firing a 7-under 63 on Saturday at Crans-Sur-Sierre Golf Club, Casey will enter Sunday at the Omega European Masters with a three-shot lead.

The last time Casey won a tournament of any sort was the 2021 Dubai Desert Classic. A lot has changed in pro golf since the last time Casey hoisted a trophy. The former World No. 3 left for LIV Golf in 2022. As a member of the Bryson DeChambeau-fronted Crushers, Casey won $31.8 million but never won a solo title, losing twice in a playoff. His last major championship appearance came at the 2022 Open Championship, and his last DP World Tour top 10 was at the Porsche Singapore Classic in 2024.

Golf.title: Add spin to your greenside chip shots with this simple technique
Golf.summary: GOLF Top 100 Teacher Jeff Smith explains the simple technique you can use to add spin to your greenside chip shots. The post Add spin to your greenside chip shots with this simple technique appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Every rec player wants to hit chip shots that take one hop and stop on a dime. Good news: It’s easier than it looks. The key is combining an open clubface with a downward angle of attack, and both are achievable with a few simple setup adjustments.

Start by grabbing your highest-lofted wedge and positioning the ball slightly forward in your stance, just below your lead eye. To promote a steeper attack angle, use a modified grip: place all five fingers of your trail hand on the club, then set the index finger of your lead hand over the pinkie of your trail hand to create a reverse overlap. Finally, rotate your trail hand slightly on top of the grip to encourage a more descending angle of attack.

Golf.title: 'Brainless of me': Early scooped putt leads to Walker Cup rules drama
Golf.summary: The 51st Walker Cup started with a meaningful short miss by the World No. 1 and some rules drama after an early scooped putt. The post ‘Brainless of me’: Early scooped putt leads to Walker Cup rules drama appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
The first session of the 51st Walker Cup at Lahinch Golf Club wasn’t short on drama. While the Americans are the clear favorites on paper, they face their stiffest test in some time against a Great Britain and Ireland team that is hungry to end Team USA’s five-tournament winning streak. Saturday morning’s foursomes session opened with World No. 1 amateur Preston Stout and Ethan Fang facing Stuart Grehan and Eliot Baker. The two teams traded blows for 15 holes, with Grehan and Baker taking a 1-up lead with three holes to play. But the Americans won 16 and 17 to reach the final hole in position to put an early point on the board.

After GB&I got in with a birdie four on the par-5 18th, Stout had a short birdie putt to tie the hole and win the match for the Americans. But his attempt slid past the hole, and GB&I salvaged a big half-point to open the competition.

As LIV Golf's future remains uncertain, professional golfer Peter Uihlein entered to compete in the DP World Tour Q-School, but he failed to show up to his third round tee-time. He started the event poorly, shooting a 74 and a 73 in the first two rounds respectively. When he was not at the tee on Friday, the event disqualified him off the leaderboard. Prior to his disqualification, he stood at 66th place and required a 19th place finish at least to advance further in the competition.

Many of those involved with LIV Golf like Uihlein are still awaiting news about their future. They need to plan contingencies unless LIV Golf 2.0, the next stage of the startup, fails to launch. Fellow LIV Golfers Luis Masaveu and Jose Luis Ballester are also participating in the event to qualify for DP World Tour status.

Golf.title: 2026's winning PGA Tour irons prove 1 thing: Blades still rule
Golf.summary: Nearly half of the 2026 PGA Tour FedEx Cup events were won by players with blade irons. Check out the full list of the winningest irons. The post 2026’s winning PGA Tour irons prove 1 thing: Blades still rule appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Remember at the beginning of the season when Rory McIlroy switched into a set of cavity-back irons, and more pros were switching out of blades seemingly every week? Not only did McIlroy switch back to his TaylorMade RORS Proto blades before his season debut at Pebble Beach and ultimately used them to win his second-straight Masters, the first five events of the PGA Tour season were also won by blade players.

Ultimately, blade players won 17 of the FedEx Cup regular season’s 37 events, a not-so-insignificant share. Players still value the precision and control offered by muscle back irons en masse on the PGA Tour.

Golf.title: LIV Golf pro is booted from DP World Tour Q-School for rules violation
Golf.summary: LIV Golf pro Peter Uihlein was booted from a DP World Tour first-stage qualifying school event due to a rules violation. The post LIV Golf pro is booted from DP World Tour Q-School for rules violation appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Peter Uihlein, who has played in LIV Golf tournaments since 2023, played two rounds at a DP World Tour first-stage qualifying school event this week and was disqualified. Uihlein’s DQ came at Huddersfield Golf Club in Huddersfield, England. He opened with rounds of four-over 74 and three-over 73, then was booted from the event after he failed to show for his third round, Bunkered’s Josh Lees reported.

The disqualification comes as the future of LIV Golf remains unclear. Two weeks ago, the league finished its fifth season of play, but it’s now trying to manage the loss of its primary backer, the Saudi Arabia Public Investment Fund. LIV CEO Scott O’Neil has said the league has received a signed term sheet with a lead investor, but has yet to name it, saying there’s “a very compressed timeline to get the deal done.”

Golf.title: New Zealand has become the ultimate golf dream trip. Here's why
Golf.summary: New Zealand has more golf courses per capita than any country other than Scotland, in a setting of unrivaled serenity and beauty. The post New Zealand has become the ultimate golf dream trip. Here’s why appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
On the world clock, New Zealand is well ahead of the United States. But North American golfers have been catching up. They’ve come to recognize the country as a must-visit, magnetic for the quality and diversity of its courses, the beauty of its landscapes and the welcoming spirit of its people.

That awareness wasn’t born overnight. It began stirring decades ago with the opening of Kauri Cliffs and Cape Kidnappers, luxurious resorts whose seaside layouts, stunning scenery and A-list accommodations remain emblems of New Zealand’s coastal splendor. The more recent arrival of marquee properties like Tara Iti and Te Arai — which combined to deliver three new courses to GOLF’s World Top 100 list — attracted next-level attention that was further magnified by the Covid golf boom. As the spotlight brightened on the North Island, it radiated outward, illuminating a golf scene of remarkable depth and range.

Golf.title: Testing the YouTube famous Takomo Irons. (Hint: They're impressive)
Golf.summary: The curiosity around Takomo irons has been loud. We wanted to find out why — and the results were very impressive The post Testing the YouTube famous Takomo Irons. (Hint: They’re impressive) appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I’ll just start here: I was late to the Takomo party. I knew the name. I’d seen the irons. I’d seen them all over YouTube and Instagram. I knew Takomo was one of those direct-to-consumer brands that had managed to build a pretty serious following without playing by the traditional golf-equipment rulebook. But knowing about something and actually hitting it are two very different things. There are plenty of golf clubs I’ve looked at, read about and formed an opinion on before ever putting one behind a ball. Then you actually hit them and realize the opinion you had was based on absolutely nothing. Which, to be fair, is kind of how the internet works.

So when I finally got some time with the Takomo irons, I went into it with one question: What’s the catch? Because golf equipment has conditioned us to think that way. If an iron looks premium, feels premium and performs like the stuff hanging on the wall at your local golf shop, we generally expect the price tag to reflect it. That’s just how this has worked for a long time. Good golf equipment costs good golf-equipment money.

Golf.body:
The U.S. Walker Cup team is now “bouncing around,” its captain, Nathan Smith, says. And his players’ stomachs, it appears, have mostly stopped rumbling. On Thursday, two days before this weekend’s amateur event, that features a 10-man American team meeting a 10-man Great Britain and Ireland team at Ireland’s Lahinch Golf Club, Golf Channel’s Brentley Romine reported that multiple Americans were fighting “stomach issues.” Ethan Feng and William Jennings, Romine said, did not practice on Thursday, and three players didn’t attend that night’s banquet.

At a Friday press conference, though, Smith said every player would be ready for Saturday, though the Americans’ first alternate, Max Herendeen, has been contacted and is on “standby” — though he’s not on site.

Golf.title: A muni made me wait 30 mins on an empty course. Was that fair?
Golf.summary: In its quest to enforce the rules, the pro shop at a California muni lost sight of the bigger picture and alienated a customer. The post A muni made me wait 30 mins on an empty course. Was that fair? appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
I recently made a tee time at my local muni for the first twilight spot of the afternoon. I arrived at the course about 35 minutes early, paid my green fee and was on the putting green when I noticed that the 1st hole was wide open. I spoke to the starter, who told me I could go. But as I stepped up to the tee, the woman who’d checked me in burst from the pro shop and yelled at me to stop. Because I’d paid the discounted twilight rate, she said, I’d have to wait until twilight officially began. Never mind that there were no groups waiting to tee off. I looked plaintively at the starter, who shrugged. He was outranked. I tried to reason with the pro shop staffer, but she insisted that I couldn’t start my round. And so I waited for another 30 minutes, with the course empty in front of me and no other golfers teeing off.

To say that I was irritated is an understatement. I’m a regular at the course and the staffer’s decision struck me as spiteful and small-minded. Was I wrong to be annoyed? As we all know, rules are rules, and they’re meant to be followed. But sometimes they can also be harmlessly broken. Let’s say you’re playing a friendly match with a pal at a poorly conditioned course, and his ball lands in a footprint in the bunker. When he asks if he can move his ball without penalty, you say sure. Have you violated the letter of the law? Technically, yes. Have you made a reasonable decision? Also, yes. On the course, as off it, common sense and context should be our guides.
Golf.copy:
I recently made a tee time at my local muni for the first twilight spot of the afternoon. I arrived at the course about 35 minutes early, paid my green fee and was on the putting green when I noticed that the 1st hole was wide open. I spoke to the starter, who told me I could go. But as I stepped up to the tee, the woman who’d checked me in burst from the pro shop and yelled at me to stop. Because I’d paid the discounted twilight rate, she said, I’d have to wait until twilight officially began. Never mind that there were no groups waiting to tee off. I looked plaintively at the starter, who shrugged. He was outranked. I tried to reason with the pro shop staffer, but she insisted that I couldn’t start my round. And so I waited for another 30 minutes, with the course empty in front of me and no other golfers teeing off.

To say that I was irritated is an understatement. I’m a regular at the course and the staffer’s decision struck me as spiteful and small-minded. Was I wrong to be annoyed? As we all know, rules are rules, and they’re meant to be followed. But sometimes they can also be harmlessly broken. Let’s say you’re playing a friendly match with a pal at a poorly conditioned course, and his ball lands in a footprint in the bunker. When he asks if he can move his ball without penalty, you say sure. Have you violated the letter of the law? Technically, yes. Have you made a reasonable decision? Also, yes. On the course, as off it, common sense and context should be our guides.

Golf.body:
As uncertainty around the future of LIV Golf continues to swirl, many of the league’s players are doing all they can to secure playing rights for the 2027 season. While the likes of Jon Rahm and Tyrrell Hatton will have little concern about picking up starts on the DP World Tour, others are having to work a bit harder. That includes their Legion XIII teammate Caleb Surratt, who has entered a couple of HotelPlanner Tour events in recent weeks, and the trio of Luis Masaveu, Josele Ballester and Peter Uihlein, who all teed up in this week’s first stage of the DP World Tour’s grueling Q School experience.

For nearly five decades, there has been one universally agreed upon poster boy for effortless golf: Fred Couples. Beginning in the late ’80s, Couples’ on-course cool was buoyed by his apparel partnership with Ashworth, the laidback, SoCal brand founded by its namesake designer, John Ashworth. Player and polo were a perfect match.

Ashworth left the brand in 1997, only to return in 2024. Needless to say, when it comes to guidance for de-stressed on-course dressing, there’s only one guy for the job. Here are Ashworth’s keys for feeling effortless, because even the king of apparel cool would say that’s way more crucial than looking the part.

Golf.body:
After months of relative quiet, the attention of President Trump’s various building projects in Washington D.C. has turned to one of the district’s municipal courses, albeit with little certainty about the administration’s official plans.

This is the increasingly popular case of East Potomac Golf Links, a 36-hole muni property in the heart of D.C. that Trump has sought to renovate into an 18-hole championship golf course. In late June, President Trump targeted Sept. 1 as the official start date for construction on the course, and while heavy machinery arrived on-site this week, that date has now passed without much proof of significant course alterations.

Golf.title: 1 answer to golf's amateur debate was on display at the U.S. Women's Mid-Am
Golf.summary: Ally Shepherd won the U.S. Women's Mid-Amateur on Thursday in New Jersey, ending a week filled with debate about golf's amateur status. The post 1 answer to golf’s amateur debate was on display at the U.S. Women’s Mid-Am appeared first on Golf .
Golf.body:
Ivy Shepherd’s putt fell on the 14th hole on Thursday at the U.S. Women’s Mid-Amateur and the tears fell soon after. It’d been a long, turbulent journey for Shepherd — one that had brought her to the heights of the collegiate amateur circuit and the doldrums of competitive golf. Now, for a few fleeting moments, it was complete.

She was a U.S. Women’s Mid-Am champion, and she was headed to the U.S. Women’s Open. “It’s awesome. It’s the longest freaking Women’s Open qualifier in the history of the world. But it’s cool,” Shepherd said. “All that is just awesome, you know, results and rewards for a long week of competitive golf for somebody who is going to end up winning it. Again, just tons of gratitude. Yeah, I feel very, very blessed.”

Golf.title: Jon Rahm’s LIV Golf Future Faces Uncertain Cliff
Golf.summary: Jon Rahm’s LIV Golf Future Faces Uncertain Cliff Yahoo Sports
Golf.body:
Jon Rahm stands at a crossroads that could define the rest of his career. The two-time major champion's future with LIV Golf looks shaky as the league tries to secure new funding. Reports suggest the breakaway tour might not keep him. This isn't just a small contract dispute. It involves a massive $150 million sum still owed to the Spanish star. As the league restructures, the man many called their flagship player might be walking away. The situation creates a ripple effect across professional golf, leaving fans wondering where the 31-year-old will play next season.

When Rahm jumped to the rebel tour in late 2023, he signed a deal loaded with cash. Per multiple reports, he is still owed around $150 million from that multi-year contract. That figure makes his position unique and complicated. As LIV Golf fights to bring in a new lead investor, reportedly BC Partners, the league's financial math changes. His contract now looks out of bounds for the new owners. Losing such a high-profile talent would be a huge blow to the league's credibility. LIV Golf CEO Scott O'Neil admitted the stakes were high. To reach and complete this transaction is the sole focus of our efforts. Without the players, that becomes very difficult, O'Neil said, as reported by reports. The pressure is on to close the deal while keeping stars like Rahm happy.

Badminton.title: The Triumph of Process
Badminton.summary: The Triumph of Process BWF World Championships
Badminton.body:
France’s two-gold haul at the BWF World Championships 2026 might have surprised the world, but for two of its prime architects, the results were simply affirmation of the quality of processes that had been put in place.

In the immediate aftermath of France’s unprecedented triumphs last month, both Cyrille Gombrowicz, National Technical Director of Federation Francaise de Badminton (FFBaD), and singles coach Kestutis Navickas had the bearing of men who had executed a plan to its logical conclusion. Far from being overwhelmed by the occasion, they spoke of how their historic victories had come about in the course of a process, rather than any particular innovation or burst of inspiration.

Satwiksairaj Rankireddy and Chirag Shetty defeated China’s He Jiting and Ren Xiangyu 11-21, 21-13, 21-17 in the China Masters 2026 final on Sunday to claim their 10th BWF World Tour title.

The victory extended the Indian pair’s head-to-head record against He and Ren to 3-0. He Jiting and Ren Xiangyu made a blistering start, racing to a 5-0 lead as their sharp play at the net and powerful smashes put the Indians under pressure. Rankireddy and Shetty got on the board but struggled to close the gap, with the Chinese pair finding the lines consistently to lead 11-5 at the interval.

Badminton.title: Farewell to Titus Kurniadi
Badminton.summary: Farewell to Titus Kurniadi BWF Corporate
Badminton.body:
BWF mourns the passing of long-time administrator Titus Kurniadi on 31 August 2026 at the age of 89. Titus Kurniadi with 1992 women’s singles Olympic champion Susi Susanti. Kurniadi served the BWF (then IBF) Council from 1986 to 1994, almost all the time as an influential Chair of Finance and Member of the Chairman’s Board. Kurnaidi also contributed immensely to Indonesian badminton as Treasurer and Foreign Affairs representative for many years.

He served at a period when the IBF received its first substantial income from the Olympic Games in Barcelona and could begin to invest substantially in the future. Kurniadi’s words helped to convince a hesitant Council to introduce the World Team Championships for the Sudirman Cup by offering on behalf of PBSI the trophy. He oversaw the creation of this treasure that incorporates elements of Indonesian history, legend, and badminton heritage.

Badminton.title: China Masters: Super 750 Glory at First Asking
Badminton.summary: China Masters: Super 750 Glory at First Asking BWF World Tour
Badminton.body:
Sumire Nakade and Miyu Takahashi needed just one shot at the HSBC BWF World Tour Super 750 level to make history. The Japanese women’s pair continued their remarkable debut season at LI-NING China Masters 2026, beating fellow Super 750 debutants Bao Li Jing/Cao Zi Han 21-18 21-18 to claim their first title at this level.

“It feels unbelievable,” the 22-year-old Nakade said after the breakthrough triumph, while Takahashi, 24, admitted she was “very happy” despite a “tense final”. The victory adds another chapter to a sublime run for the pair, who have lost just twice since winning their first HSBC BWF World Tour event at the Orleans Masters in March. They have since lifted the US and Taipei Open titles, making it four victories from six World Tour tournaments.

The biggest shock came in men’s singles, where Hong Kong China’s Jason Gunawan stunned top seed and newly crowned world No.1 Jonatan Christie 21-16 21-16 in their first meeting.

“I know my opponent had more pressure. I’m the underdog so I just did my best to win every point,” said Gunawan. The 22-year-old revealed preparation was deliberately uncomplicated, with his coach encouraging him to attack rather than allow Christie to settle.

Competitor News.summary: England to make major change to kit after striking sponsorship deal with Lloyds Bank The Independent
Competitor News.body:
The back of England rugby’s shirts will carry a sponsor’s name for the first time after Lloyds Bank struck a lucrative new partnership with the Rugby Football Union (RFU). The multi-million pound per year deal will see the bank’s famous black horse logo and name emblazoned above the player names on the kits of England’s men and women, beginning with the Red Roses’ clash with Australia in Manchester this weekend.

The agreement will see Lloyds becomes one of the RFU’s leading partners, with significant investment expected into the community game, and is another significant boost to the union’s finances.

Competitor News.title: Turkish Airlines to Replace Standard Chartered as Liverpool FC Main Partner in Landmark 2027 Deal
Competitor News.summary: Turkish Airlines to Replace Standard Chartered as Liverpool FC Main Partner in Landmark 2027 Deal Ministry of Sport
Competitor News.body:
Liverpool Football Club has announced a transition, naming Turkish Airlines as its new main club partner from June 1, 2027. The agreement will see the airline’s branding feature prominently on the front of the men’s, women’s, and Academy match shirts starting from the 2027-28 season, marking the club’s first front-of-shirt partner change in 17 years. Highlighting the milestone, chief commercial officer at LFC, Ben Latty, said: “This is a milestone announcement for us and we are delighted to welcome Turkish Airlines as our main club partner from June 2027.”

The move sees the Reds move on from Standard Chartered as their front-of-shirt presence, although the London-based bank will not be leaving the club entirely. Having served as the principal sponsor since 2010, Standard Chartered will transition into a role as a global partner.

- Getty Images SportEnd of the Standard Chartered eraBen Latty, Liverpool's chief commercial officer, expressed the significance of the change. "This is a milestone announcement for us and we are delighted to welcome Turkish Airlines as our main club partner from June 2027," Latty said to the club's official website. "The front of the Liverpool shirt holds a special place in the history of our club. "Turkish Airlines is a globally recognised organisation with an extensive international network, and we look forward to beginning our partnership and building a strong relationship together, with already strong foundations built from those special memories back in 2005." Latty also took the time to praise the outgoing main sponsor, adding: "This announcement also provides an opportunity to recognise the extraordinary contribution Standard Chartered has made to Liverpool FC over the past 17 years. "They have been an important part of our journey through an exceptional period in the club’s history, and we are delighted that Standard Chartered will remain part of the Liverpool FC family as a global partner from June 2027. “As we prepare for this transition, we look forward to this new season and welcoming Turkish Airlines as our main club partner from June 2027."

The campaign will focus on the initiatives the bank has run as part of its sponsorship, including its school sports week, ticket giveaways, support for Olympic athletes and backing of the torch relay.
